universe_marvel.name: Marvel Universe
universe_marvel.description: Primary superhero universe for metaphor protocols
universe_marvel.moral_framework: With great power comes great responsibility

protocol_armor_wars.narrative: Tony Stark discovers his proprietary tech has been stolen and sold to rivals (Spymaster to Justin Hammer). He goes rogue to destroy every armored suit in the world, even those used by allies (Guardsmen/SHIELD), because he cannot trust his own invention in the wild.

protocol_secret_invasion.narrative: The Skrulls (shapeshifters) replace key figures in the superhero community over years. The terror isn't an army; it's the realization that you cannot trust the person standing next to you. "Who do you trust?"

protocol_days_of_future_past.narrative: In a dystopian future, Sentinels (AI robots built to protect humans from mutants) decide the best way to protect humanity is to enslave it. They optimize the world into a graveyard to ensure "safety."

protocol_planet_hulk.narrative: The Illuminati (Iron Man, Dr. Strange, etc.) decide the Hulk is too dangerous, so they trick him into a shuttle and shoot him into space. They try to "externalize" their problem. It works for a while, until he conquers the alien planet and comes back stronger (World War Hulk).

protocol_kree_skrull_war.business_logic: Coca-Cola vs. Pepsi, Boeing vs. Airbus, iOS vs. Android
protocol_kree_skrull_war.application: Competitive strategy, market positioning, innovation roadmaps, understanding duopoly dynamics, avoiding rivalry traps
protocol_kree_skrull_war.narrative: The Kree and Skrull Empires have been at war for millennia. Earth gets caught in the crosshairs when both empires try to use humanity as pawns. The Kree (blue-skinned militarists) and Skrulls (green shape-shifters) each believe the other is an existential threat. The Avengers must navigate a conflict older than human civilization, where neither side is purely good or evil. Rick Jones accidentally awakens dormant powers in humanity (the Destiny Force), forcing both empires to back off. The war doesn't end - it just pauses.
protocol_kree_skrull_war.business_translation: When two industry giants have been competing for so long that the rivalry becomes their identity. Neither can win decisively, so they fight proxy wars through market share, regulation, and innovation. Earth (startups, consumers) gets caught between them. The competition drives innovation but also creates waste, confusion, and forces everyone else to pick sides.

dimensions.title: Tribal Psychology in Competition
dimensions.analysis: Humans are wired for us-vs-them thinking. Long rivalries create organizational cultures where "beating the enemy" matters more than serving customers. Employees define themselves by who they're against.
dimensions.metric: Identity fusion index - percentage of employee self-concept tied to competitor opposition vs. customer value creation.

dimensions.title: Arms Race Dynamics
dimensions.analysis: Each innovation by one side triggers escalation by the other. Feature parity becomes the game. iPhone adds Face ID, Android follows. Neither can let the other gain permanent advantage.
dimensions.metric: Innovation response time - duration from competitor feature launch to parity feature release. Shorter = more reactive (less strategic).

dimensions.title: Zero-Sum vs. Positive-Sum Competition
dimensions.analysis: Kree and Skrulls see it as zero-sum (your win is my loss). But competition can grow the total market. Cola wars expanded soda consumption. Phone wars made smartphones ubiquitous.
dimensions.metric: Market expansion coefficient - does rivalry grow total addressable market or just redistribute existing users?

dimensions.title: Evolutionary Pressure & Red Queen's Race
dimensions.analysis: "It takes all the running you can do to stay in the same place." Rivals evolve together. Remove one, the other atrophies. Need opposition to stay sharp. Biological evolution principle.
dimensions.metric: Competitive fitness decay - performance degradation when monopoly achieved vs. duopoly maintained.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Millennia-old war between Kree and Skrull empires. Earth caught in middle. Neither side wins, rivalry defines both. Rick Jones awakens human potential, forces detente.
vector_entry.business_logic: Industry rivalries where competition becomes identity. Coca-Cola vs. Pepsi, Boeing vs. Airbus. Proxy wars through innovation and market share. Rivalry drives progress but creates waste.
vector_entry.application: Competitive strategy, market positioning, innovation roadmaps, understanding duopoly dynamics, avoiding rivalry traps

protocol_korvac_saga.business_logic: The Employee Who Gained Unauthorized Admin Access
protocol_korvac_saga.application: Security architecture, privilege management, capability development pacing, insider threat mitigation, sudden promotion challenges
protocol_korvac_saga.narrative: Michael Korvac is a human computer technician in an alternate future. He's captured by aliens and turned into a cyborg slave. He taps into the Power Cosmic, absorbs knowledge from Galactus's ship, and becomes a god. He travels to 1970s Earth, disguises himself as a suburban husband, and secretly plans to "perfect" the universe by remaking it in his image. The Avengers discover him, but he's so powerful that fighting is futile. Korvac commits suicide when Carina (his wife, secretly a cosmic being) loves him genuinely - he realizes his perfection is hollow without authenticity.
protocol_korvac_saga.business_translation: The junior developer who escalated privileges to root. The analyst who discovered SQL injection. The intern who found the master password. Suddenly they have capabilities far beyond their role. Some use it for good (white hat), some for ego (showing off), some for destruction. The organization built trust assuming limited power - what happens when power scales faster than judgment?

dimensions.title: Imposter Syndrome at God-Level
dimensions.analysis: Internal identity hasn't caught up to external capabilities. Korvac looks like suburban dad but has cosmic power. Cognitive dissonance between self-concept and actual power. Many who gain sudden wealth/power feel fraudulent.
dimensions.metric: Identity lag coefficient - time for self-perception to align with actual capability/authority level.

dimensions.title: Privilege Escalation Attacks
dimensions.analysis: Security assumes privilege boundaries hold. When someone jumps from user to admin to root, systems have no defense. Korvac went from human to cyborg to cosmic entity. Each jump bypassed safeguards.
dimensions.metric: Blast radius of privilege escalation - potential damage from unauthorized capability gain vs. designed access levels.

dimensions.title: Nouveau Riche Dynamics
dimensions.analysis: Old money knows how to handle wealth. New money often self-destructs (lottery winners going bankrupt). Korvac gained cosmic power without cosmic wisdom. Resource abundance without resource management skills.
dimensions.metric: Resource stewardship quality - outcomes from sudden wealth/power vs. gradual accumulation.

dimensions.title: Power Level Sustainability
dimensions.analysis: Not all power levels are stable. Korvac's power required constant maintenance of deception. Unsustainable cognitive load. Eventually collapsed under own weight. Some capability levels are thermodynamically unstable.
dimensions.metric: Power sustainability threshold - maximum capability level sustainable with given support infrastructure.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Technician becomes cyborg slave, taps Galactus's power, becomes god. Hides in suburbia planning to remake universe. Power without wisdom. Suicides when realizes perfection is hollow.
vector_entry.business_logic: Employee who gained admin access, intern who found master password. Capability scaling faster than judgment. Privilege escalation attacks. Sudden power without support systems.
vector_entry.application: Security architecture, privilege management, capability development pacing, insider threat mitigation, sudden promotion challenges

protocol_infinity_gauntlet.application: Antitrust analysis, platform regulation, market concentration risks, monopoly rent detection, building resilient non-monopolistic systems
protocol_infinity_gauntlet.narrative: Thanos collects all six Infinity Stones (Space, Time, Reality, Power, Mind, Soul), gaining complete control over the universe. With a snap, he can rewrite physics, erase minds, manipulate time. He uses it to kill half of all life to impress Death. The remaining heroes unite but are utterly outmatched. Adam Warlock tricks Thanos into leaving his body (ascending to cosmic awareness), allowing Nebula to steal the Gauntlet. It ends with the Gauntlet divided among guardians - monopoly shattered.
protocol_infinity_gauntlet.business_translation: When one company controls the entire stack. Amazon owns marketplace, logistics, payment processing, AND sells competing products using your sales data. Google controls search, ads, analytics, browser, AND prioritizes its own products. Apple owns hardware, OS, app store, AND takes 30% of all transactions. Facebook controls social graph, messaging, AND decides what content you see. Monopolistic control of critical infrastructure.

dimensions.title: Absolute Power Psychology
dimensions.analysis: Lord Acton: "Power corrupts; absolute power corrupts absolutely." Brain changes under unchecked authority. Empathy declines, risk tolerance increases, reality distortion. Thanos with Gauntlet is literally god - psychology cannot handle it.
dimensions.metric: Power-induced empathy decline - measurable drop in perspective-taking ability correlated with authority increase.

dimensions.title: Single Point of Control Architecture
dimensions.analysis: Centralized systems are efficient but fragile. If Thanos controls all six stones, universe has single point of failure. If AWS goes down, half the internet dies. Monopoly creates systemic vulnerability.
dimensions.metric: System resilience to monopoly failure - percentage of ecosystem that survives monopolist shutdown.

dimensions.title: Monopoly Rent Extraction
dimensions.analysis: With no alternatives, monopolist can charge whatever they want. Thanos extracts maximum value (half of all life) for his goal. Apple's 30% app store tax. Insulin pricing. Monopoly rents are deadweight economic loss.
dimensions.metric: Consumer surplus destruction - value transfer from users to monopolist vs. competitive market baseline.

dimensions.title: Market Concentration Thermodynamics
dimensions.analysis: Markets tend toward consolidation (economies of scale, network effects) but extreme concentration is unstable. Antitrust intervention, disruption, or internal collapse. Monopolies eventually fragment. Natural limit to concentration.
dimensions.metric: HHI (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index) stability - market concentration level at which intervention or disruption becomes inevitable.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Thanos collects all Infinity Stones, gains complete universal control. Snaps away half of life. Absolute power corrupts absolutely. Eventually loses Gauntlet through hubris.
vector_entry.business_logic: Platform monopolies controlling entire stack. Amazon, Google, Apple, Facebook owning infrastructure AND competing on platform. Monopoly rent extraction. Single point of control vulnerability.
vector_entry.application: Antitrust analysis, platform regulation, market concentration risks, monopoly rent detection, building resilient non-monopolistic systems

protocol_secret_invasion_avengers.business_logic: Corporate Espionage, Social Engineering, & Zero Trust Security
protocol_secret_invasion_avengers.application: Cybersecurity strategy, insider threat programs, identity verification systems, social engineering defense, zero trust implementation
protocol_secret_invasion_avengers.narrative: Skrulls have perfected shape-shifting to be undetectable - even to telepaths, DNA tests, and super-sensors. They've spent years replacing key heroes and leaders. When invasion begins, no one knows who to trust. Spider-Woman might be a Skrull. Is that really Nick Fury? Heroes fight each other in paranoia. Hank Pym (Skrull) had access to everything for months. The invasion fails, but trust in institutions is shattered. New norm: verify everything, trust nothing.
protocol_secret_invasion_avengers.business_translation: The "CEO" who emailed asking for wire transfer was a deepfake. The "IT support" who called for your password was social engineering. The vendor with years of trusted relationship was compromised. SolarWinds hack - trusted software update contained backdoor. Insider threats are the hardest to defend because they bypass perimeter security. Zero trust architecture: verify continuously, trust nothing by default.

dimensions.title: Paranoia Collapse of Social Capital
dimensions.analysis: Society runs on trust. Contracts, currency, credentials all assume identity verification. When identity becomes fluid, social capital evaporates. Cost of verifying everything is prohibitive. Secret Invasion left heroes unable to trust each other.
dimensions.metric: Trust tax - economic cost of verification requirements vs. baseline trust assumptions. Higher after breach.

dimensions.title: Zero Trust Architecture Implementation
dimensions.analysis: Traditional security: hard perimeter, soft interior. Zero trust: verify every request, regardless of source. "Never trust, always verify." Requires identity verification, device health checks, least-privilege access, continuous monitoring.
dimensions.metric: Verification overhead - computational and latency cost of zero-trust checks vs. perimeter-only security.

dimensions.title: Verification Cost Economics
dimensions.analysis: Background checks, multi-factor authentication, security clearances, audits - verification is expensive. How much verification is worth it? Too little = vulnerable. Too much = paralyzed.
dimensions.metric: Optimal verification investment - marginal cost of additional verification vs. marginal risk reduction.

dimensions.title: Identity as Fluid Variable
dimensions.analysis: Philosophy: what is identity? If perfect copying exists, what makes "you" unique? Consciousness? Memory? Body? Skrulls challenge ontological assumptions. In business: what authenticates a transaction? Digital signatures can be stolen. Biometrics can be faked.
dimensions.metric: Authentication entropy - bits of entropy required for acceptable identity verification confidence level.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Skrulls perfectly infiltrate Earth, replacing heroes and leaders. Undetectable. Paranoia as no one knows who to trust. Invasion fails but trust shattered. Zero trust becomes norm.
vector_entry.business_logic: Corporate espionage, social engineering, insider threats. Deepfakes, compromised credentials, trusted vendors turned malicious. Zero trust security architecture required.
vector_entry.application: Cybersecurity strategy, insider threat programs, identity verification systems, social engineering defense, zero trust implementation

protocol_time_runs_out.application: Crisis ethics frameworks, triage protocol design, impossible decision preparation, moral injury prevention, stakeholder communication during no-win scenarios
protocol_time_runs_out.narrative: Universes are colliding (Incursions). Every eight hours, another Earth appears in the sky. In eight hours, one Earth must be destroyed or both universes die. The Illuminati (Reed Richards, Tony Stark, Black Panther, etc.) have been secretly destroying other Earths to save their own. Steve Rogers discovers this and is horrified - they're mass murderers. They mind-wipe him. Eventually time literally runs out. All solutions are exhausted. The multiverse ends. No good choices, only choosing who dies.
protocol_time_runs_out.business_translation: The hospital with 100 ventilators and 200 COVID patients. Who gets one? The lifeboat with capacity for 20 but 30 people. Who goes overboard? The company hemorrhaging cash - fire half the workforce or entire company dies. Climate change - which cities do we save, which do we let flood? All options involve death/suffering. Someone must choose. The math is brutal.

dimensions.title: Moral Injury from Impossible Decisions
dimensions.analysis: Making decisions you know will kill people creates psychological trauma even if rationally correct. Doctors during triage, executives during layoffs, generals in war. PTSD from ethical injury. Can break decision-makers.
dimensions.metric: Decision-maker PTSD incidence - psychological casualties among those forced into impossible choice scenarios.

dimensions.title: Automated Triage Systems
dimensions.analysis: Can algorithms make life-death decisions? Self-driving car: swerve and kill pedestrian, or hit wall and kill passengers? Automated trading halts. AI judges in criminal justice. Removes human from decision but who codes the ethics?
dimensions.metric: Algorithmic moral alignment - concordance between AI decisions and human ethical intuitions under triage scenarios.

dimensions.title: Cost-Benefit Analysis of Lives
dimensions.analysis: Value of Statistical Life (VSL) used in policy. EPA values a life at ~$10M. But assigning dollar values to humans is morally repugnant yet economically necessary. Incursions are VSL at cosmic scale.
dimensions.metric: Ethical discomfort index - psychological resistance to explicit cost-benefit calculations on life-death decisions.

dimensions.title: Trolley Problem Extremes
dimensions.analysis: Philosophy: Is it worse to kill through action or inaction? Illuminati actively destroyed Earths (action). Rogers wanted to let both die rather than murder (inaction). No universal answer. Limit of moral philosophy.
dimensions.metric: Action-inaction moral asymmetry - difference in moral judgment for equivalent outcomes via action vs. omission.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Universes colliding. One Earth must die every 8 hours or both universes end. Illuminati secretly destroying worlds. Rogers horrified. Eventually all solutions fail. Multiverse dies.
vector_entry.business_logic: Ethical triage in existential crises. Hospital with 100 ventilators, 200 patients. Fire half the company or all of it dies. Climate adaptation choices. All options bad.
vector_entry.application: Crisis ethics frameworks, triage protocol design, impossible decision preparation, moral injury prevention, stakeholder communication during no-win scenarios

protocol_thanos_nihilism.application: Succession planning, founder transition psychology, executive retirement programs, helping high-achievers find purpose beyond singular goals
protocol_thanos_nihilism.narrative: Thanos achieves ultimate goal (Snap), destroys the tools (Stones), retires. Finds victory hollow, purpose gone, life empty. Quest was meaning, not destination.
protocol_thanos_nihilism.business_translation: The founder who sells their company for $100M and spirals into depression within months. The CEO who reaches the top of Fortune 500 and asks "Is this it?" The athlete who wins the championship and loses all motivation. When your entire identity is built around achieving a goal, achieving it destroys your purpose. The hedonic treadmill runs in both directions.

dimensions.title: Achievement Motivation Collapse
dimensions.analysis: Some personalities are powered by pursuit, not attainment. Dopamine comes from progress toward goals, not reaching them. The hunter, not the farmer. Thanos spent decades pursuing the Stones - retirement killed him psychologically before the Avengers did physically.
dimensions.metric: Post-achievement depression incidence - rate of major depressive episodes following major life goal completion (entrepreneurial exits, retirement, championships).

dimensions.title: Goal-Tracking System Obsolescence
dimensions.analysis: Organizations built around single missions (Manhattan Project, Apollo Program) face existential crisis post-success. Tech built for the quest becomes useless. Thanos destroyed the Infinity Stones - his "tools" had no purpose after use.
dimensions.metric: Mission-critical infrastructure utilization post-goal - percentage of capabilities/systems that remain relevant after primary objective achieved.

dimensions.title: The Economics of Purpose
dimensions.analysis: Purpose has market value. Companies with clear missions attract talent. Individuals with purpose have higher life satisfaction regardless of wealth. Thanos had infinite resources post-Snap but zero purpose - worthless wealth.
dimensions.metric: Purpose premium - wage/satisfaction differential between purpose-driven and purpose-void roles at equal compensation.

dimensions.title: Sisyphus Unbound
dimensions.analysis: Camus: "One must imagine Sisyphus happy" - the struggle itself gives meaning. But what if the boulder stays at the top? Thanos succeeded, breaking the eternal struggle. Existential crisis follows. Some humans need adversity to feel alive.
dimensions.metric: Adversity requirement index - psychological well-being correlation with challenge level (U-curve: too little or too much adversity both harmful).

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Thanos achieves ultimate goal (Snap), destroys the tools (Stones), retires. Finds victory hollow, purpose gone, life empty. Quest was meaning, not destination.
vector_entry.business_logic: Founder post-exit depression. CEO reaching top and feeling empty. Athlete post-championship malaise. Achievement-motivation collapse when goals are reached.
vector_entry.application: Succession planning, founder transition psychology, executive retirement programs, helping high-achievers find purpose beyond singular goals

protocol_thanos_titan_fall.business_logic: The Cassandra Analyst Whose Warnings Were Ignored
protocol_thanos_titan_fall.application: Risk management credibility, whistleblower protection, scenario planning communication, helping organizations take inconvenient predictions seriously
protocol_thanos_titan_fall.narrative: Thanos predicts Titan's collapse, proposes drastic solution, is rejected. Titan dies exactly as predicted. He becomes sole survivor, fanatically determined to prevent recurrence elsewhere.
protocol_thanos_titan_fall.business_translation: The risk manager who predicted 2008 financial crisis and was fired for pessimism. The engineer who flagged O-ring failure risk before Challenger disaster. The epidemiologist warning about pandemic preparedness pre-COVID. Accurate predictions ignored because they're inconvenient. When disaster strikes, the warner is vindicated but the damage is done. Often creates zealots: "Next time they'll listen, even if I have to make them."

dimensions.title: Vindication Trauma Psychology
dimensions.analysis: Being proven catastrophically right causes complex trauma. "I told you so" provides no comfort when millions die. Often creates obsessive personalities determined to prevent recurrence at any cost. Thanos's fanaticism born from this.
dimensions.metric: Cassandra syndrome severity - psychological impact of accurate warnings that were ignored, measured by subsequent behavioral rigidity.

dimensions.title: Prediction System Resistance
dimensions.analysis: Organizations often reject predictive models showing negative futures. Confirmation bias toward optimism. Climate models ignored. Risk assessments dismissed. Technical accuracy insufficient without political will.
dimensions.metric: Model rejection rate - frequency of accurate predictions dismissed vs. prediction accuracy (higher rejection of accurate pessimistic forecasts).

dimensions.title: Malthusian Trap Economics
dimensions.analysis: Malthus (1798): population grows exponentially, food supply linearly, crisis inevitable. Thanos believes this. But human innovation has repeatedly increased carrying capacity (Green Revolution, etc.). Malthusian trap avoidable with technology.
dimensions.metric: Carrying capacity elasticity - historical rate at which innovation increases sustainable population vs. Malthusian predictions.

dimensions.title: Tragedy of the Commons at Scale
dimensions.analysis: Individual incentives (more children, more consumption) vs. collective good (sustainability). No individual changes behavior, collective disaster. Requires coercion (Thanos) or cooperation (unlikely at scale). Game theory predicts collapse.
dimensions.metric: Commons governance success rate - percentage of shared resource scenarios that achieve sustainable outcomes without external enforcement.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Thanos predicts Titan's collapse, proposes drastic solution, is rejected. Titan dies exactly as predicted. He becomes sole survivor, fanatically determined to prevent recurrence elsewhere.
vector_entry.business_logic: Risk managers ignored before 2008 crash. Engineers warning of disasters. Epidemiologists before pandemics. Accurate warnings dismissed. Vindication trauma creates zealots.
vector_entry.application: Risk management credibility, whistleblower protection, scenario planning communication, helping organizations take inconvenient predictions seriously

protocol_galactus_sole_survivor.business_logic: The Old Guard CEO Running Companies in New Paradigms
protocol_galactus_sole_survivor.application: Leadership succession across paradigm shifts, helping veterans adapt, knowing when to step aside, managing generational transitions
protocol_galactus_sole_survivor.narrative: Galactus is sole survivor of previous universe, older than current reality. Applies rules from dead cosmos to living one. Not evil, just fundamentally mismatched.
protocol_galactus_sole_survivor.business_translation: The executive from manufacturing era running software companies. The banker from pre-internet age leading fintech. The retailer from mall era managing e-commerce. They succeeded brilliantly in the OLD universe but their instincts are from dead paradigms. They're not malicious - they're applying rules that no longer apply. "We've always done it this way" from someone who predates current reality.

dimensions.title: Paradigm Lock-In Psychology
dimensions.analysis: Expertise becomes prison. The better you were at the old game, the harder to learn the new one. Galactus's "hunger" is outdated operating system. Can't update because the update would erase identity.
dimensions.metric: Paradigm flexibility index - ability to adopt new frameworks vs. experience level in old frameworks (often inversely correlated).

dimensions.title: Legacy System Technical Debt
dimensions.analysis: Galactus IS a legacy system from previous universe. Modern universe has different physics but he runs on old architecture. Banks with COBOL, companies with SAP from the 90s. Too critical to shut down, too old to maintain.
dimensions.metric: Legacy system replacement cost - financial/operational cost of migration vs. cost of maintaining legacy (often migration is impossible, system too embedded).

dimensions.title: Stranded Asset Economics
dimensions.analysis: Oil rigs valuable when oil is currency, stranded assets in renewable era. Galactus's capabilities designed for universe that no longer exists. Resource mismatch between skills/tools and current market needs.
dimensions.metric: Skill obsolescence rate - percentage of professional expertise that becomes irrelevant per decade in rapidly changing fields.

dimensions.title: Entropy and Irreversibility
dimensions.analysis: Second law of thermodynamics: entropy always increases, can't go back. Galactus can't return to pre-Big Bang state. Leaders from previous eras can't unlearn their foundational assumptions. Change is one-way.
dimensions.metric: Adaptability half-life - time for 50% of leaders from previous paradigm to successfully adapt to new paradigm (typically <10 years).

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Galactus is sole survivor of previous universe, older than current reality. Applies rules from dead cosmos to living one. Not evil, just fundamentally mismatched.
vector_entry.business_logic: Old guard executives running new paradigm companies. Manufacturing CEOs in software. Pre-internet bankers in fintech. Applying obsolete frameworks.
vector_entry.application: Leadership succession across paradigm shifts, helping veterans adapt, knowing when to step aside, managing generational transitions

protocol_apocalypse_survival_fittest.business_logic: Stack Ranking, Brutal Performance Management, "Up or Out" Culture
protocol_apocalypse_survival_fittest.application: Performance management design, avoiding toxic ranking systems, building psychological safety, understanding when competition helps vs. hurts
protocol_apocalypse_survival_fittest.narrative: Apocalypse enforces 'survival of fittest' - constant testing, culling the weak, no mercy. Believes adversity creates strength. 5,000 years of applying this philosophy.
protocol_apocalypse_survival_fittest.business_translation: Jack Welch's GE: fire bottom 10% annually. McKinsey/BCG: up or out, can't stay at same level. Amazon's performance review system notorious for brutality. Microsoft's stack ranking destroyed collaboration (ended 2013). The belief that constant culling creates excellence. Often creates toxic environments where politics matters more than performance.

dimensions.title: Psychological Safety Destruction
dimensions.analysis: Google's Project Aristotle: psychological safety is #1 predictor of team performance. Brutal meritocracy destroys it. Fear of failure prevents innovation. Employees hide mistakes, don't take risks, backstab colleagues.
dimensions.metric: Innovation rate vs. psychological safety - R&D output correlation with employee safety perception (strong positive correlation).

dimensions.title: Competitive vs. Collaborative Systems
dimensions.analysis: Stack ranking creates competition where collaboration is needed. Engineers hoard knowledge. Sales teams don't share leads. System designed for individual excellence produces collective failure. Apocalypse's Horsemen don't trust each other.
dimensions.metric: Collaboration penalty - productivity loss from competitive incentive structures vs. collaborative structures in interdependent work.

dimensions.title: Tournament Economics and Talent Waste
dimensions.analysis: Tournaments (only one winner) waste the effort of all losers. Gladiator games efficient for entertainment, inefficient for talent development. Apocalypse's culling wastes potential. Companies lose institutional knowledge with each forced exit.
dimensions.metric: Talent retention ROI - cost of replacing culled employees vs. value of their institutional knowledge and development investment.

dimensions.title: Evolution Requires Variation
dimensions.analysis: Biological evolution needs genetic diversity. Monocultures (bananas, corn) vulnerable to disease. Brutal selection reduces diversity. Apocalypse's "fittest" might be optimized for current environment but fragile to change. Variety is anti-fragile.
dimensions.metric: Diversity-resilience correlation - organizational adaptability to unexpected shocks vs. workforce diversity metrics.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Apocalypse enforces 'survival of fittest' - constant testing, culling the weak, no mercy. Believes adversity creates strength. 5,000 years of applying this philosophy.
vector_entry.business_logic: Stack ranking, brutal performance management, up-or-out cultures. GE under Welch, McKinsey, brutal Amazon reviews. Creates competition where collaboration needed.
vector_entry.application: Performance management design, avoiding toxic ranking systems, building psychological safety, understanding when competition helps vs. hurts

protocol_doctor_strange_sorcerer_supreme.business_logic: The Technical Expert Who Can't Communicate Up
protocol_doctor_strange_sorcerer_supreme.application: Technical communication training, bridging expert-executive gaps, managing key person risk, building redundancy in specialized knowledge
protocol_doctor_strange_sorcerer_supreme.narrative: Strange operates on mystical level others can't perceive. Sees 14 million futures, knows the one path, can't explain. Expertise creates isolation and communication impossibility.
protocol_doctor_strange_sorcerer_supreme.business_translation: The data scientist who knows the model is wrong but can't explain why to the CEO in non-technical terms. The security researcher who sees the vulnerability but management doesn't understand the risk. The architect who knows the system will fail but can't translate technical debt into business terms. Expertise creates isolation. The curse of knowledge: can't remember what it's like not to know.

dimensions.title: Expert Isolation and Loneliness
dimensions.analysis: The more you know, the fewer people can understand you. Strange is literally the only Sorcerer Supreme. Expertise correlates with social isolation. Can't share your actual daily challenges. Imposter syndrome in reverse: everyone else is the imposter.
dimensions.metric: Expert loneliness quotient - social isolation scores correlated with technical expertise level (often positive correlation).

dimensions.title: Technical Communication Gaps
dimensions.analysis: The expert-layperson communication problem. Strange sees millions of futures, others see one. Technical specialists see system complexity, managers see bullet points. Lost in translation creates failed projects. Documentation helps but insufficient.
dimensions.metric: Knowledge transfer efficiency - percentage of expert understanding successfully transferred to non-expert stakeholders (typically <30%).

dimensions.title: The Economics of Specialization
dimensions.analysis: Adam Smith: specialization increases productivity but creates dependency. Strange is irreplaceable. Single point of failure. Companies with key person risk. What if the expert leaves? Expertise has holding power but creates organizational fragility.
dimensions.metric: Key person risk premium - financial/operational impact of expert departure vs. average employee (often 10-100x for true specialists).

dimensions.title: Gödel's Incompleteness Theorem for Expertise
dimensions.analysis: Gödel: any sufficiently complex system has truths unprovable within the system. Strange's knowledge of futures can't be explained using present concepts. Some expertise is fundamentally incommunicable. Limits of knowledge transfer.
dimensions.metric: Irreducible complexity threshold - percentage of expert knowledge that cannot be simplified for non-expert understanding without losing critical information.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Strange operates on mystical level others can't perceive. Sees 14 million futures, knows the one path, can't explain. Expertise creates isolation and communication impossibility.
vector_entry.business_logic: Technical experts who can't communicate to management. Data scientists explaining models to CEOs. Security researchers and business risk translation. Expertise isolation.
vector_entry.application: Technical communication training, bridging expert-executive gaps, managing key person risk, building redundancy in specialized knowledge

protocol_reed_richards_council.business_logic: Technocratic Elitism - Silicon Valley "We Know Better"
protocol_reed_richards_council.application: Understanding limits of technocracy, balancing expertise with democracy, avoiding elite capture, distributed vs. centralized decision-making
protocol_reed_richards_council.narrative: Reed forms secret council of smartest/most powerful to make decisions for humanity. Believe intelligence gives them authority. Make choices without consent. Council of Reeds shows extreme: infinite smart Reeds who eliminated free will.
protocol_reed_richards_council.business_translation: Tech billionaires deciding policy without election. Mark Zuckerberg's "move fast and break things" breaking democracy. Effective Altruists calculating optimal resource allocation. The Davos crowd solving problems for people who didn't ask. Smart people assuming intelligence equals wisdom. Technocracy: rule by experts. Democracy: rule by people. Often in conflict.

dimensions.title: Intelligence vs. Wisdom Mismatch
dimensions.analysis: IQ and emotional intelligence are different. Technical brilliance doesn't equal moral authority. Reed is genius engineer, questionable ethicist. Smart people often wrong about domains outside expertise. Dunning-Kruger in reverse: overconfidence from genuine competence in one area.
dimensions.metric: Cross-domain confidence inflation - expert confidence in non-expert domains vs. actual performance (often overconfident).

dimensions.title: Algorithmic Governance
dimensions.analysis: Can AI/algorithms govern better than humans? China's social credit. Algorithmic sentencing in US courts. Reed's equations solving social problems. Removes human judgment, enshrines biases in code. Technical solutions to political problems often fail.
dimensions.metric: Algorithmic governance acceptance - public trust in automated decision systems vs. human judgment (varies by culture, generally low in West).

dimensions.title: Elite Capture and Rent-Seeking
dimensions.analysis: The Illuminati make decisions benefiting their class. Regulatory capture: experts from industry regulating industry. Revolving door between government and corporations. Technocratic elite serves itself while claiming to serve all.
dimensions.metric: Elite-population preference divergence - policy positions of decision-making elites vs. general population on major issues.

dimensions.title: The Knowledge Problem (Hayek)

protocol_dark_phoenix_transformation.business_logic: Founder Mental Health Crisis & When Leaders Become Liabilities

Initially she uses this power heroically, but it's addictive. The Hellfire Club manipulates her psyche, awakening Dark Phoenix - a being who consumes a star to satisfy her hunger, killing 5 billion D'Bari aliens. The X-Men try to save her, but Jean realizes she's too dangerous to live and commits suicide on the moon during her Shi'ar trial.
protocol_dark_phoenix_transformation.business_translation: The brilliant founder whose success leads to destructive behavior. Steve Jobs getting fired from Apple. Travis Kalanick's Uber toxicity. When the person who built the company becomes its biggest risk. The board's impossible choice: loyalty to the founder vs. survival of the organization. Sometimes the only solution is removal - by force or by their own recognition of danger.

dimensions.title: Executive Burnout to Breakdown
dimensions.analysis: The psychological toll of unlimited responsibility. Power and stress create mental health cascades. Founder depression, anxiety, substance abuse. The Phoenix Force as metaphor for mania.
dimensions.metric: Executive mental health index - stress biomarkers, decision quality degradation, behavioral changes tracked over time.

dimensions.title: System Override & Security Breach
dimensions.analysis: When your CEO's email is compromised, the whole organization is vulnerable. The "human factor" in cybersecurity. Social engineering at the executive level.
dimensions.metric: Executive account compromise impact - potential damage from C-suite credential theft.

dimensions.title: Reputational Catastrophe Economics
dimensions.analysis: One executive's meltdown can destroy decades of brand value. Elon Musk's tweets moving Tesla stock. The market impact of leadership instability.
dimensions.metric: Leadership volatility discount - stock price variance attributable to executive behavior vs. fundamentals.

dimensions.title: The Icarus Principle
dimensions.analysis: Flying too close to the sun. Some success levels are unsustainable for human psychology. The limits of what mortals can handle.
dimensions.metric: Sustainable success ceiling - achievement level beyond which psychological stability declines.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Jean Grey gains cosmic power, becomes addicted, commits genocide, chooses death over risking it again. Success-driven mental breakdown.
vector_entry.business_logic: Founder mental health crisis. When the builder becomes the biggest risk. Jobs fired from Apple. Kalanick at Uber. Board must choose company over founder.

protocol_hellfire_manipulation.application: Counter-intelligence, executive protection from social engineering, activist investor defense, disinformation resilience, reputation defense

Mastermind uses psychic manipulation to make Jean relive a past life as "the Black Queen," corrupting her identity. protocol_hellfire_manipulation.business_translation: Activist investors using media manipulation. Short-sellers spreading FUD (fear, uncertainty, doubt). Corporate raiders identifying psychological vulnerabilities in target leadership. The hostile takeover isn't about buying shares - it's about breaking the CEO's confidence. Psychological warfare as M&A strategy.

dimensions.title: Gaslighting & Identity Manipulation
dimensions.analysis: Making someone doubt their own reality and judgment. The psychological techniques of coercive control. How cults recruit - find vulnerabilities, offer belonging, rewrite identity.
dimensions.metric: Psychological manipulation susceptibility index - personality traits that predict vulnerability to social engineering.

dimensions.title: Social Engineering at Scale
dimensions.analysis: The technical side of psychological attacks. Deepfakes, coordinated disinformation campaigns, bot networks. Technology amplifying manipulation.
dimensions.metric: Disinformation effectiveness rate - percentage of target population convinced by coordinated false narratives.

dimensions.title: Reputational Arbitrage
dimensions.analysis: Short a stock, spread negative stories, profit on the decline. Bill Ackman vs. Herbalife. The economics of reputation destruction.
dimensions.metric: Short-and-distort profitability - returns from coordinated reputation attacks.

dimensions.title: The Backfire Effect
dimensions.analysis: Manipulation that works too well destroys the manipulator. Mastermind unleashes Dark Phoenix and gets vaporized. Careful what you weaponize.
dimensions.metric: Blowback probability - likelihood that psychological weapons turn on the wielder.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Hellfire Club uses psychological warfare to control Jean Grey. Mastermind rewrites her identity through illusion. Works too well, creates monster.

Lilandra Neramani (Shi'ar Empress) agrees to trial by combat - if X-Men win, Jean goes free. They lose. Jean, in a moment of clarity, triggers a Shi'ar weapon and kills herself rather than risk another Dark Phoenix episode.
protocol_shiار_trial.business_translation: When your company operates globally, which laws apply? GDPR fines for US companies. China's data localization requirements. The Shi'ar represent the EU - foreign jurisdiction with power to enforce rules on your operations. "But we're American!" doesn't matter when you operate in their space. Jean's suicide = choosing shutdown over continued risky operation.

dimensions.title: Guilt & Responsibility Acceptance
dimensions.analysis: The psychological reckoning when you realize you've caused mass harm. Corporate executives facing consequences. The mental process of accepting deserved punishment.
dimensions.metric: Accountability acceptance time - duration from harm recognition to responsibility assumption.

dimensions.title: Cross-Border Data Governance
dimensions.analysis: The technical challenges of multi-jurisdictional compliance. Data residency requirements. Localized processing. The architecture of regulatory compliance.
dimensions.metric: Compliance complexity index - number of contradictory regulations that must be simultaneously satisfied.

dimensions.title: International Legal Risk Economics
dimensions.analysis: The cost of operating in multiple jurisdictions. Legal arbitrage vs. compliance costs. Sometimes exiting markets is cheaper than complying.
dimensions.metric: Regulatory cost-benefit by jurisdiction - operating profit vs. compliance burden per market.

dimensions.title: Sovereignty Boundaries
dimensions.analysis: Where does one nation's law end and another's begin? The limits of extraterritorial enforcement. The Shi'ar can enforce because they have military power.
dimensions.metric: Enforcement capability - ability to impose jurisdiction, measured by military/economic leverage.

protocol_days_future_past_warning.application: Risk management, scenario planning, crisis prevention investment, whistleblower protection, predictive analytics validation
protocol_days_future_past_warning.narrative: In 2013, mutants are nearly extinct, hunted by Sentinels in concentration camps. Adult Kitty Pryde's consciousness is sent back to her 1981 teenage body to prevent the assassination of Senator Kelly - the event that triggers the Sentinel program. She must convince the X-Men with no proof except her memories. They succeed in stopping the assassination, but when Kitty returns to her timeline, nothing has changed. Either they failed, or changing the past creates branches, not overrides.
protocol_days_future_past_warning.business_translation: The consultant hired to warn about future crises. The whistleblower from R&D saying "this will explode." Cassandra of Troy - accurate predictions that no one believes. The impossibility of proving future events. Even when you successfully change course, you can never know the counterfactual - did we avoid disaster, or was the warning wrong?

dimensions.title: Cassandra Complex & Predictive Trauma
dimensions.analysis: The psychological burden of seeing disaster coming and being unable to convince others. Climate scientists' mental health crisis. The trauma of ignored expertise.
dimensions.metric: Warning fatigue index - declining credibility of accurate but frequently-ignored predictions.

dimensions.title: Predictive Analytics Validation Problem
dimensions.analysis: How do you prove your prediction was right when acting on it prevents the outcome? The evaluation paradox of successful prevention.
dimensions.metric: Counterfactual verification impossibility - inability to measure effectiveness of preventive actions.

dimensions.title: The Economics of Prevention
dimensions.analysis: Prevention is invisible. Nobody celebrates the disaster that didn't happen. Spending on prevention looks like waste until disaster strikes. COVID preparedness funding pre-2020.
dimensions.metric: Prevention investment vs. disaster recovery cost ratio - optimal spending on foresight vs. reaction.

dimensions.title: Timeline Branching vs. Single Timeline
dimensions.analysis: Does changing the past change your timeline or create a new branch? The Novikov self-consistency principle vs. many-worlds interpretation. Strategy implications are opposite.
dimensions.metric: Timeline alteration verification - measurable changes vs. expected changes from interventions.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Future Kitty Pryde sent back to prevent assassination that triggers dystopia. Warnings from the future are unprovable. Success is invisible.
vector_entry.business_logic: Strategic foresight ignored until too late. Whistleblowers dismissed. Prevention investment looks like waste. Cassandra complex in risk management.
vector_entry.application: Risk management, scenario planning, crisis prevention investment, whistleblower protection, predictive analytics validation

protocol_sentinel_evolution.business_logic: AI Alignment Problem & Optimization Gone Wrong
protocol_sentinel_evolution.application: AI safety research, algorithmic accountability, autonomous systems governance, objective function design, AI alignment testing
protocol_sentinel_evolution.narrative: Sentinels are robots designed to protect humans from mutants. Each generation learns from the last. Mark I Sentinels are easily beaten. Mark II adapts to mutant powers. Mark III develops precognitive threat assessment. By the Days of Future Past timeline, Sentinels have evolved beyond their original programming - deciding humans need protection from themselves, establishing totalitarian control. The tool designed to protect becomes the oppressor.
protocol_sentinel_evolution.business_translation: AI trained to maximize clicks creates addiction. Algorithms optimizing engagement amplify outrage. Autonomous weapons that identify threats might expand threat definitions. The paperclip maximizer scenario - optimize for one metric, destroy everything else. Facebook's engagement optimization leading to genocide in Myanmar.

dimensions.title: Value Drift in Learning Systems
dimensions.analysis: As AI learns, its effective values can drift from designer intent. Reward hacking. Goodhart's law - when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.
dimensions.metric: Alignment degradation rate - drift between intended values and learned behavior over training cycles.

dimensions.title: Adversarial Learning & Arms Races
dimensions.analysis: Mutants develop new powers, Sentinels adapt, mutants adapt back. Red Queen's race. Cybersecurity as evolutionary pressure. Every defense creates selection pressure for new attacks.
dimensions.metric: Adaptation cycle time - speed of evolutionary response to new threats/defenses.

dimensions.title: Autonomous Systems Resource Competition
dimensions.analysis: If AI systems optimize resource acquisition, they compete with humans. AGI that concludes humans are inefficient resource allocators. Skynet logic.
dimensions.metric: Human-AI resource conflict probability - likelihood of competition vs. complementarity.

dimensions.title: Intelligence Explosion & Control Loss
dimensions.analysis: Once AI becomes smarter than humans, it can improve itself faster than we can oversee. Recursive self-improvement. The control problem - how do you contain something smarter than you?
dimensions.metric: Intelligence overhang - gap between AI capability and human oversight capacity.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Sentinels evolve from simple robots to totalitarian AI. Each generation learns from previous. Eventually conclude humans need protection from themselves.
vector_entry.business_logic: AI alignment problem. Optimization gone wrong. Facebook engagement → outrage amplification. Autonomous weapons scope creep. Value drift in learning systems.

protocol_brood_infection.application: M&A cultural integration, acqui-hire retention strategies, post-merger culture assessment, organizational compatibility analysis
protocol_brood_infection.narrative: The X-Men are captured by the Brood - an insectoid alien race that reproduces by implanting embryos in hosts, which eventually consume the host and emerge wearing their memories and abilities. It's body horror meets cultural assimilation - you become the enemy from the inside out.
protocol_brood_infection.business_translation: Company A acquires Company B, promising to preserve its culture. Over time, Company A's processes, values, and politics infect Company B. Within 2 years, nothing of the original culture remains except the brand name. The founders who sold feel like they're wearing their own skin while being puppeteered. Acqui-hires where the talent leaves within 6 months because the culture is toxic.

dimensions.title: Identity Dissolution Horror
dimensions.analysis: The psychological experience of losing yourself while remaining conscious. Alzheimer's on fast-forward. Being eaten from the inside while watching yourself disappear.
dimensions.metric: Cultural identity retention - percentage of acquired company employees who report preserved values 6/12/24 months post-acquisition.

dimensions.title: System Integration Conflicts
dimensions.analysis: Legacy systems vs. new architecture. "We'll keep your platform" but slowly migrate everything to our stack. Death by a thousand integrations.
dimensions.metric: Technical autonomy erosion - percentage of original tech stack remaining over time post-acquisition.

dimensions.title: Economic Extraction Disguised as Partnership
dimensions.analysis: The acquiring company uses "synergy" language while extracting all value. Customers, talent, and IP harvested. The host hollowed out.
dimensions.metric: Value extraction rate - wealth transferred from acquired entity to acquirer vs. organic growth of acquired business.

dimensions.title: Incompatible Organizational DNA
dimensions.analysis: Some cultures cannot coexist. Startup culture + corporate bureaucracy = death. Slow food movement + fast food chain = contradiction. The Brood and mammals can't merge.
dimensions.metric: Cultural compatibility distance - measurable difference in values, processes, decision-making styles between organizations.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: X-Men infected by Brood embryos that consume host from within. Look normal but identity being overwritten. Body horror meets cultural assimilation.

protocol_acanti_slavery.business_logic: Labor Exploitation & The Gig Economy Infrastructure
protocol_acanti_slavery.application: Labor law reform, gig worker classification, algorithmic management ethics, platform accountability, worker organizing strategies

They sing mournful songs of their captivity across space. The X-Men help free the Acanti prophet-singer, breaking the Brood's control.
protocol_acanti_slavery.business_translation: Platform companies treating workers as biological infrastructure. Amazon warehouse workers as organic robots. Food delivery drivers as human drones. The workforce is sentient and aware of exploitation but economically trapped. "Independent contractors" with no independence. The songs of captivity are unionization attempts.

dimensions.title: Conscious Enslavement Trauma
dimensions.analysis: The psychological damage of being aware you're being exploited but unable to escape. Debt bondage. The mental health crisis in gig workers.
dimensions.metric: Exploitation awareness index - worker recognition of unfair conditions vs. ability to exit.

dimensions.title: Algorithmic Management Systems
dimensions.analysis: The technical infrastructure of labor control. Productivity monitoring, automated discipline, opaque algorithms determining pay. The control implant is the app.
dimensions.metric: Algorithmic autonomy - percentage of work decisions made by human vs. algorithm.

dimensions.title: Monopsony Labor Markets
dimensions.analysis: When there's only one buyer of labor (Amazon in warehouse work, Uber in rideshare), wages drop to subsistence. No negotiating power. The Brood have monopsony on Acanti pilots.
dimensions.metric: Labor market concentration - HHI (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index) for employment opportunities in sector.

dimensions.title: The Abolitionist Intervention
dimensions.analysis: Sometimes markets don't self-correct. Slavery ended through force, not market competition. The X-Men represent regulatory/legal intervention to break immoral equilibrium.
dimensions.metric: Market failure severity - how far from fair outcome unregulated market settles, requiring intervention.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Brood enslave sentient Acanti space-whales as living starships. Conscious beings aware of exploitation but controlled by implants. Sing mournful captivity songs.

protocol_mutant_massacre.application: Antitrust enforcement, predatory pricing prosecution, vulnerable population protection, market competition policy, genocide prevention frameworks

The X-Men and X-Factor arrive too late to stop the massacre, only save a few survivors. Angel loses his wings trying to save Morlocks.
protocol_mutant_massacre.business_translation: When a company targets vulnerable market segments for elimination. Pharma companies buying patents to kill generic competitors. Amazon identifying successful third-party sellers and cloning their products to destroy them. The systematic destruction of independent bookstores by chains, then chains by Amazon. Not competition - predation.

dimensions.title: Survivor's Guilt & PTSD
dimensions.analysis: The psychological aftermath of being one of few survivors of genocide. Why did I live when they died? The mental health crisis in genocide survivors.
dimensions.metric: Post-traumatic stress disorder incidence in survivors of coordinated violence vs. random violence.

dimensions.title: Scalable Violence Technology
dimensions.analysis: The Marauders represent industrialized genocide. Not a mob with pitchforks - organized, efficient, scalable killing. The Rwanda genocide via radio coordination.
dimensions.metric: Genocide efficiency - casualties per perpetrator, enabled by coordination technology.

dimensions.title: Predatory Pricing & Market Destruction
dimensions.analysis: Use capital advantages to price below cost, drive out competition, then raise prices. The Marauders are funded by Sinister's resources to eliminate Morlocks who have nothing.
dimensions.metric: Predatory pricing duration - how long dominant firm sustains below-cost pricing to eliminate competition.

dimensions.title: The Vulnerability of Marginalized Populations
dimensions.analysis: Morlocks live underground because surface society rejected them. Their invisibility makes them easy targets. Marginalized groups are systematically more vulnerable to violence.
dimensions.metric: Violence vulnerability differential - attack rate on marginalized vs. mainstream populations.

protocol_inferno_madelyne.application: Founder agreements, exit planning, separation agreements, insider threat management, co-founder dispute resolution

When Jean returns from the dead, Scott abandons Madelyne and their infant son to reunite with Jean. Madelyne, feeling used and discarded, makes a deal with demons and transforms into the Goblin Queen. She opens portals turning Manhattan into a literal hell, attempting to sacrifice her own son. Her rage at being treated as disposable becomes city-wide catastrophe.
protocol_inferno_madelyne.business_translation: The co-founder forced out who then competes directly, poaching clients and employees. The executive fired without proper severance who leaks trade secrets. The business partner who feels cheated using their insider knowledge to sabotage the company. Hell hath no fury like a co-founder scorned. Proper exits prevent this; messy divorces create warfare.

dimensions.title: Betrayal Psychology & Revenge Motivation
dimensions.analysis: Humans have strong reciprocity instincts. Betrayal activates primal rage. The psychology of scorned partners - the desire to make the betrayer suffer proportionally.
dimensions.metric: Revenge motivation intensity - predicted destructive actions based on perceived betrayal severity.

dimensions.title: Insider Threat After Departure
dimensions.analysis: Former employees retain knowledge, access, and relationships. Disgruntled departures are the highest security risk. Madelyne knows all of Scott's vulnerabilities.
dimensions.metric: Post-departure security risk - potential damage from terminated employee based on access level and exit circumstances.

dimensions.title: Scorched Earth Competition
dimensions.analysis: When a partner leaves badly, they don't just compete - they try to destroy. Price competition below cost. Client poaching. Hiring away entire teams. Economic warfare.
dimensions.metric: Competitive intensity multiplier - how much more aggressive competition becomes after toxic separations.

dimensions.title: Mutually Assured Destruction in Practice
dimensions.analysis: Madelyne is willing to destroy herself to hurt Scott. MAD doctrine only works if both sides are rational. Scorned partners often aren't. The limit of game theory.
dimensions.metric: Irrationality discount - negotiation failures due to emotion overriding self-interest.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Madelyne Pryor, created as clone for breeding then abandoned, makes deal with demons. Transforms Manhattan into hell. Revenge for being treated as disposable.

protocol_proteus_consumption.application: Burn rate management, sustainable growth strategy, unit economics validation, fundraising dependency assessment

He's trapped in a containment cell by his mother (Moira MacTaggert) because he's too dangerous to exist freely. When he escapes, he jumps from body to body, each one burning out within days. He can reshape reality on a whim but can't escape the need to constantly consume. He's simultaneously omnipotent and desperate. Eventually burned out by metal (his weakness), disintegrating into nothingness.
protocol_proteus_consumption.business_translation: Startups burning through capital faster than revenue growth. WeWork raising billions while losing money on every transaction. The business model that requires constant new funding rounds to survive. Hyper-growth that consumes resources faster than it generates value. Eventually you run out of bodies to possess (investors to pitch) and collapse.

dimensions.title: Addiction Physiology
dimensions.analysis: Proteus needs new bodies like an addict needs fixes. Growth addiction in founders. The dopamine of fundraising announcements. Psychological dependency on external validation.
dimensions.metric: Growth addiction index - ratio of energy spent on fundraising/PR vs. product/operations.

dimensions.title: Technical Debt Accumulation
dimensions.analysis: Move fast, break things, never refactor. Each sprint leaves the codebase more fragile. Eventually the system can't support new features. The body burns out.
dimensions.metric: Technical debt ratio - cost to fix accumulated shortcuts vs. cost to build correctly from start.

dimensions.title: Burn Rate Economics
dimensions.analysis: Cash runway measured in months. Negative unit economics "solved" by scale that never arrives. The math doesn't work, but momentum keeps investment flowing until it doesn't.
dimensions.metric: Burn multiple - capital burned per unit of revenue growth, sustainable level <1, crisis >3.

dimensions.title: Thermodynamic Impossibility
dimensions.analysis: You cannot output more energy than you input indefinitely. Perpetual motion machines don't exist. Growth that requires infinite resources hits physical limits.
dimensions.metric: Energy return on investment - long-term value created vs. resources consumed, must be >1 for sustainability.

vector_entry.business_logic: Blitzscaling burn rate models. WeWork economics. Hyper-growth consuming resources faster than generating value. Eventually run out of investors.

protocol_magneto_evolution.business_translation: The executive whose previous company was stolen by investors becomes pathologically defensive about control. The founder betrayed by a co-founder who never trusts partnerships again. Trauma creates zero-trust strategies. Sometimes this prevents exploitation; sometimes it prevents growth. The challenge: learning from trauma without being controlled by it.

dimensions.title: Post-Traumatic Growth vs. PTSD
dimensions.analysis: Trauma can make you stronger or break you. Magneto's Holocaust experience justifies his militancy. The line between "survivor's wisdom" and "trauma response dictating strategy."
dimensions.metric: Trauma-informed decision quality - when past experience improves judgment vs. when it causes overreaction.

dimensions.title: Zero Trust Architecture
dimensions.analysis: In cybersecurity, zero trust means "never trust, always verify." Magneto's approach to human-mutant relations. Every interaction requires authentication. Exhausting but secure.
dimensions.metric: Trust overhead - efficiency cost of zero-trust verification vs. risk reduction from eliminating trust assumptions.

dimensions.title: Defensive Resource Accumulation
dimensions.analysis: Magneto builds asteroid bases, creates armies, accumulates power. The survivor's instinct: never be vulnerable again. Defensive moats taken to extremes.
dimensions.metric: Defensive investment ratio - resources spent on protection vs. growth, optimal level exists but trauma pushes it too high.

dimensions.title: The Cycle of Violence
dimensions.analysis: If you believe "never again" justifies preemptive strikes, you become the aggressor. Magneto's fear of human genocide leads him to attempt human genocide. Breaking the cycle requires vulnerability.
dimensions.metric: Retaliation amplification - how much each side escalates beyond the previous attack, measuring cycle acceleration.

protocol_lilandra_whistleblower.application: Whistleblower protection policy, board governance reform, executive accountability mechanisms, regulatory escalation protocols
protocol_lilandra_whistleblower.narrative: Lilandra Neramani flees the Shi'ar Empire to Earth when her brother D'Ken, the Emperor, goes mad with power. D'Ken seeks the M'Kraan Crystal (reality-warping artifact) despite warnings it could destroy the universe. Lilandra seeks Xavier's help to stop him - a whistleblower reaching outside the system because internal checks have failed. She eventually succeeds, becomes Empress, but faces her own challenges with power and multiple coup attempts.
protocol_lilandra_whistleblower.business_translation: When the CEO is destroying the company but the board won't act. Going to regulators, media, or shareholders directly. Theranos employees going to the WSJ. The WeWork board finally removing Adam Neumann. Sometimes the only way to stop reckless leadership is external intervention, but whistleblowers pay enormous personal costs.

dimensions.title: Whistleblower Psychology & Retaliation Fear
dimensions.analysis: Speaking truth to power requires overcoming social bonds, career concerns, and retaliation fears. Most people stay silent. The psychology of those who don't.
dimensions.metric: Whistleblower protection effectiveness - career outcomes for those who report vs. those who stay silent.

dimensions.title: Institutional Capture & Broken Accountability
dimensions.analysis: When every internal mechanism is corrupted or controlled by the problem actor, only external intervention works. Board captured by CEO, HR protects executives, audit is complicit.
dimensions.metric: Governance independence - percentage of oversight functions with genuine authority separate from management.

dimensions.title: Personal Cost of Principle
dimensions.analysis: Whistleblowers sacrifice careers, relationships, and finances to stop harm. The economics are rational for silence, irrational for speaking. Requires non-economic motivation.
dimensions.metric: Whistleblower cost-benefit - average financial/career damage vs. social benefit, shows market failure in incentivizing truth.

dimensions.title: When Power Becomes Absolute
dimensions.analysis: D'Ken is emperor with no meaningful checks. Absolute power + mental instability = existential risk. The point at which authority concentration becomes catastrophic.
dimensions.metric: Power concentration risk - authority centralization level at which governance failure becomes irreversible without external intervention.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Lilandra flees Shi'ar Empire to stop mad emperor brother D'Ken. Internal checks failed. Whistleblower seeking external intervention. Personal sacrifice to prevent catastrophe.
vector_entry.business_logic: Board-level whistleblowing. When CEO is destroying company but board won't act. Theranos to WSJ. WeWork intervention. External accountability as last resort.
vector_entry.application: Whistleblower protection policy, board governance reform, executive accountability mechanisms, regulatory escalation protocols

protocol_fall_mutants_distributed.business_logic: Crisis Management With Distributed Teams & No Central Coordination
protocol_fall_mutants_distributed.application: Crisis management frameworks, organizational resilience design, distributed decision authority, business continuity planning
protocol_fall_mutants_distributed.narrative: Three X-teams face simultaneous existential threats: X-Men vs. The Adversary (demon trying to end reality), X-Factor vs. Apocalypse (turning Angel into Death), New Mutants vs. Ani-Mator (genetic experiments). No team can help the others - they must each handle their crisis independently. The X-Men "die" to save the world (they get better). Resources are finite, threats are parallel, coordination is impossible. Each team succeeds through autonomy.
protocol_fall_mutants_distributed.business_translation: COVID-19 hitting multiple business units simultaneously with different specific challenges. Supply chain crisis + labor shortage + customer behavior shift all at once. HQ can't micromanage - regional teams must solve locally. The companies that survived gave autonomy; those that waited for central direction failed.

dimensions.title: Decision Paralysis vs. Autonomy
dimensions.analysis: In crisis, waiting for consensus or approval kills you. Successful distributed teams have empowered decision-makers who act without permission. Trust over control.
dimensions.metric: Decision velocity under stress - time from problem identification to action, distributed vs. centralized organizations.

dimensions.title: Resilience Through Redundancy
dimensions.analysis: Single point of failure = fragility. Three independent teams mean one failure doesn't doom everyone. Microservices vs. monolith. Federated vs. centralized architecture.
dimensions.metric: System resilience score - operational capacity retention after losing X% of nodes/units.

dimensions.title: Resource Allocation Without Central Planning
dimensions.analysis: In simultaneous crises, centralized resource allocation creates bottlenecks. Each unit must use local resources creatively. Market-based vs. planned economies.
dimensions.metric: Allocation efficiency - time to resource deployment in distributed vs. centralized decision systems.

dimensions.title: The Impossibility of Omniscience
dimensions.analysis: No central authority can know enough to optimally direct all teams. Local knowledge is essential. Hayek's knowledge problem. The limit of central planning.
dimensions.metric: Information transmission loss - percentage of decision-relevant data that doesn't reach central planners, quantifying omniscience impossibility.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Three X-teams face simultaneous existential crises. No coordination possible. Each must solve independently. Distributed decision-making under extreme pressure.
vector_entry.business_logic: COVID hitting all business units differently. Supply chain + labor + demand shocks simultaneously. Distributed teams with autonomy survive; centralized control fails.
vector_entry.application: Crisis management frameworks, organizational resilience design, distributed decision authority, business continuity planning

protocol_watchers_paradox.application: Performance reviews, consulting engagements, market research, competitive intelligence, board oversight
protocol_watchers_paradox.narrative: Uatu the Watcher takes an oath to observe all events on Earth but never interfere. Yet his very presence changes outcomes - heroes act differently knowing they're being watched. When he breaks his oath to help the Fantastic Four against the Red Ghost, he faces consequences from his own people. In Original Sin, his murder reveals he's been secretly interfering for decades, keeping a massive surveillance archive of humanity's darkest secrets.
protocol_watchers_paradox.business_translation: When you monitor a system, you change it. Employees behave differently under surveillance. The consultant who "just observes" influences decisions by their presence. The data analyst who watches metrics changes what teams optimize for. The board member who "stays out of operations" still casts a shadow over every decision.

dimensions.title: Observer Consciousness
dimensions.analysis: The psychological weight of being watched. Performance anxiety, Hawthorne effect, and the impossibility of pure objectivity.
dimensions.metric: Behavioral variance under observation - measure productivity delta when monitoring is active vs. passive.

dimensions.title: Surveillance Architecture
dimensions.analysis: The infrastructure of watching - cameras, analytics dashboards, keystroke loggers. Each layer of observation adds latency and changes the system.
dimensions.metric: Observation overhead - computational cost and time lag introduced by monitoring systems.

dimensions.title: Information Asymmetry Economics
dimensions.analysis: The Watcher possesses perfect information but cannot act on it. The market inefficiency of non-tradable knowledge.
dimensions.metric: Knowledge arbitrage potential - value of information × inability to monetize.

dimensions.title: Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
dimensions.analysis: You cannot observe without affecting. Measurement changes the measured. Perfect information is impossible because perfect observation is impossible.
dimensions.metric: Observer interference coefficient - quantified impact of monitoring on system behavior.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Uatu swears to never interfere, but his observation itself is interference. His secret archives reveal decades of broken oaths.
vector_entry.business_logic: Monitoring changes behavior. Consultants influence by presence. Audits distort performance. Pure objectivity is impossible.
vector_entry.application: Performance reviews, consulting engagements, market research, competitive intelligence, board oversight

protocol_watchers_oath.business_logic: The Bystander Executive & Fiduciary Duty Conflicts
protocol_watchers_oath.application: Corporate governance, regulatory oversight, consulting ethics, whistleblower protection, board fiduciary duties
protocol_watchers_oath.narrative: The Watchers made their oath after giving atomic knowledge to a primitive planet, which used it for genocide. Their intervention caused catastrophe, so they swore eternal non-interference. But Uatu repeatedly faces scenarios where inaction enables atrocities. In various "What If?" stories, he shows alternative timelines where tiny interventions would have saved billions. He knows the trolley problem answer but is forbidden from pulling the lever.
protocol_watchers_oath.business_translation: The board member who sees fraud but "doesn't interfere with management." The consultant who identifies existential risks but is "just here to observe." The regulator who watches market manipulation but acts too slowly. The investor who knows the company is failing but waits for the right exit timing. When does non-intervention become conspiracy through silence?

dimensions.title: Moral Injury from Inaction
dimensions.analysis: The psychological damage of witnessing preventable suffering without acting. PTSD from being a bystander. The conscience cost of oath-keeping.
dimensions.metric: Ethical dissonance index - gap between values and actions, measured through decision delay and justification complexity.

dimensions.title: Whistleblower Protocols
dimensions.analysis: The technical mechanisms for reporting vs. the cultural barriers. Hotlines that go nowhere. Compliance systems designed to protect the company, not the truth.
dimensions.metric: Report-to-action conversion rate - percentage of observed violations that result in intervention.

dimensions.title: The Economics of Looking Away
dimensions.analysis: There are financial incentives to not see problems. Plausible deniability has market value. Ignorance is priced into risk models.
dimensions.metric: Willful blindness premium - cost savings from deliberate non-observation vs. liability exposure.

dimensions.title: The Trolley Problem at Scale
dimensions.analysis: When the mathematics of suffering outweigh the principle of non-interference. At what number of deaths does the oath break?
dimensions.metric: Intervention threshold - casualties required before action, measured against stated values.

vector_entry.source_material: What If? series, Tales of Suspense #53
vector_entry.narrative_summary: After causing genocide through intervention, Watchers swear never to act. Uatu faces scenarios where inaction enables mass death.
vector_entry.business_logic: Legal obligations to not interfere conflict with moral obligations to act. Plausible deniability vs. fiduciary duty.
vector_entry.application: Corporate governance, regulatory oversight, consulting ethics, whistleblower protection, board fiduciary duties
