protocol_watchers_archive.application: Data privacy compliance, surveillance capitalism models, intelligence gathering ethics, HR data governance, social media content moderation
protocol_watchers_archive.narrative: Uatu's lunar base contains a perfect archive of every event on Earth - every crime, every secret, every innovation. When Nick Fury discovers this after Uatu's murder, he realizes the Watcher has footage of who killed his parents, who really shot JFK, the location of every hidden weapon. Perfect intelligence, completely unusable. The archive becomes a liability - whoever controls it has blackmail material on everyone, but using it breaks the cosmic order.
protocol_watchers_archive.business_translation: Companies collect massive behavioral data but face increasing restrictions on usage. Intelligence agencies have perfect surveillance but legal constraints. HR departments know everything about employees but can't act on information obtained improperly. The GDPR paradox: data is valuable only if actionable, but action triggers liability. Chinese social credit vs. Western privacy laws - same data, opposite philosophies.

dimensions.title: The Panopticon Effect
dimensions.analysis: When people know a perfect archive exists, behavior changes even if the archive is never used. The psychological prison of total surveillance.
dimensions.metric: Self-censorship rate - measurable decline in risky/creative behavior under total monitoring.

dimensions.title: Data Gravity & Access Control
dimensions.analysis: The technical challenge of storing everything while making nothing accessible. Encryption vs. analytics. Privacy-preserving computation that's too expensive to use.
dimensions.metric: Data utilization ratio - percentage of collected data that generates actionable insights vs. storage cost.

dimensions.title: Information as Toxic Asset
dimensions.analysis: Some knowledge is a liability. Knowing creates obligation. The archive is valuable but dangerous to own. Data breach exposure exceeds data value.
dimensions.metric: Information liability ratio - legal/PR risk of data breach vs. business value of data.

dimensions.title: The Omniscience Curse
dimensions.analysis: Perfect information is paralyzing. Every decision has visible consequences. You see all trolley problems simultaneously. God's-eye view causes decision paralysis.
dimensions.metric: Analysis paralysis index - decision velocity decline correlated with information completeness.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Uatu's lunar base archives every Earth event with perfect fidelity. Perfect intelligence, zero usage rights. A liability masquerading as an asset.
vector_entry.business_logic: Surveillance capitalism faces data governance crisis. Perfect information without action rights is a toxic asset. GDPR makes archives dangerous.
vector_entry.application: Data privacy compliance, surveillance capitalism models, intelligence gathering ethics, HR data governance, social media content moderation

protocol_tribunal_three_faces.application: ESG decision-making, stakeholder capitalism, board governance, regulatory balance, judicial review processes
protocol_tribunal_three_faces.narrative: The Living Tribunal has three faces: Equity (fairness), Necessity (pragmatism), and Vengeance (justice). All three must agree before the Tribunal acts. When Thanos assembles the Infinity Gauntlet, the Tribunal observes but doesn't intervene because Thanos represents a necessary cosmic test. Even when Adam Warlock wields the Gauntlet, the Tribunal judges him unworthy because he cannot integrate all aspects of justice. The fourth face (the cosmic one) remains blank - representing the mystery of ultimate judgment.
protocol_tribunal_three_faces.business_translation: Modern corporations must balance shareholders (Vengeance - return on capital), stakeholders (Equity - fair distribution), and operational reality (Necessity - what's actually possible). ESG frameworks try to judge companies through three lenses simultaneously. The board must balance fiduciary duty, social responsibility, and business viability. When these conflict, decisions become impossible - just like the Tribunal's paralysis.

dimensions.title: Judicial Temperament & Decision Psychology
dimensions.analysis: The mental framework required to hold multiple contradictory values simultaneously. Cognitive load of multi-objective optimization. The personality traits of supreme judges.
dimensions.metric: Value conflict resolution time - decision latency when stakeholder interests directly oppose.

dimensions.title: Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA)
dimensions.analysis: The algorithms and frameworks for balancing incommensurable values. How do you weigh profit vs. planet vs. people in a single function?
dimensions.metric: Pareto efficiency score - percentage of decisions that don't sacrifice one value for another.

dimensions.title: Allocative Justice Economics
dimensions.analysis: The resource allocation problem when fairness, efficiency, and desert all point different directions. Market outcomes vs. moral outcomes.
dimensions.metric: Gini coefficient delta - inequality measure before vs. after "fair" allocation decisions.

dimensions.title: Arrow's Impossibility Theorem
dimensions.analysis: No voting system can satisfy all fairness criteria simultaneously. Perfect justice is mathematically impossible with multiple values.
dimensions.metric: Fairness criterion violations - count of impossible-to-resolve stakeholder conflicts per decision cycle.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Living Tribunal's three faces (Equity, Necessity, Vengeance) must unanimously agree to act. Multi-value optimization causes decision paralysis.
vector_entry.business_logic: Stakeholder capitalism requires balancing shareholders, stakeholders, and operational reality. ESG creates impossible optimization problems.
vector_entry.application: ESG decision-making, stakeholder capitalism, board governance, regulatory balance, judicial review processes

protocol_tribunal_erasure.business_logic: Bankruptcy, Market Exits, and Orderly Liquidation
protocol_tribunal_erasure.application: Bankruptcy proceedings, market exit strategies, corporate restructuring, mass layoff decisions, systemic risk management
protocol_tribunal_erasure.narrative: When universes collide in the Incursion crisis, the Living Tribunal has the power to simply erase one reality to save the other. It's the ultimate triage decision - sacrifice billions to save trillions. The Beyonders eventually kill the Tribunal, proving even cosmic law can be overruled by sufficient force. The Tribunal's death represents the collapse of rules-based order into pure power dynamics.
protocol_tribunal_erasure.business_translation: Sometimes the only solution is dissolution. Chapter 7 vs. Chapter 11. The decision to shut down a business unit. Firing half the company to save the other half. The controlled demolition of a failed bank to prevent systemic collapse. The Fed's choice of which banks to save in 2008 - Bear Stearns erased, Goldman Sachs preserved.

dimensions.title: Survivor Guilt & Triage Psychology
dimensions.analysis: The mental health impact of making life-or-death allocation decisions. Who lives, who dies, and the people who choose.
dimensions.metric: Decision-maker PTSD incidence - psychological casualty rate among executives who execute mass layoffs.

dimensions.title: Bankruptcy Automation & Smart Contracts
dimensions.analysis: Can you algorithmically determine which entities should cease to exist? Automated market makers that liquidate positions. Smart contracts that self-execute shutdowns.
dimensions.metric: Algorithmic liquidation efficiency - speed and cost of automated vs. human-managed wind-downs.

dimensions.title: Creative Destruction Economics
dimensions.analysis: Schumpeter's gale - capitalism requires failure. Zombie companies drain resources from productive uses. Sometimes erasure is economically optimal.
dimensions.metric: Economic deadweight from preservation - GDP loss from keeping non-viable entities operational.

dimensions.title: The Entropy Floor
dimensions.analysis: Not everything can be saved. Some systems have passed the point of no return. Thermodynamics applies to organizations - you can't unscramble the egg.
dimensions.metric: Viability threshold - minimum resource level below which recovery is thermodynamically impossible.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Living Tribunal can erase entire realities for cosmic balance. Its death proves even ultimate law yields to sufficient force.
vector_entry.business_logic: Sometimes the only solution is orderly liquidation. Chapter 7 bankruptcy. Mass layoffs. Controlled demolition of failed institutions.
vector_entry.application: Bankruptcy proceedings, market exit strategies, corporate restructuring, mass layoff decisions, systemic risk management

protocol_galactus_devourer.application: Energy policy, extractive industries defense, growth-at-all-costs strategy, resource nationalism, climate change debates
protocol_galactus_devourer.narrative: Galactus is the sole survivor of the previous universe, transformed into a cosmic force of nature. He doesn't eat worlds out of malice - he needs their life energy to survive. He's a fundamental force, like gravity or entropy. His Herald, the Silver Surfer, scouts for suitable planets, then betrays Galactus to save Earth. Galactus explains: "I am beyond good and evil. I simply am, and I must feed."
protocol_galactus_devourer.business_translation: Oil companies don't drill to be evil - they extract because civilization runs on energy. Mining companies strip mountains because phones need rare earths. Amazon consumes retail businesses because the market demands infinite selection and two-day shipping. The "we have to do this to survive" defense. When growth is existential, externalities become acceptable collateral damage.

dimensions.title: Primal Hunger & Existential Drives
dimensions.analysis: The most basic biological imperative overrides all other considerations. Maslow's hierarchy - can't think about ethics when you're starving.
dimensions.metric: Survival urgency index - how close to existential crisis, measured by resource runway.

dimensions.title: Energy Infrastructure Dependency
dimensions.analysis: Modern civilization requires constant energy throughput. Grid collapse = societal collapse. The technical necessity of extraction.
dimensions.metric: Energy consumption growth rate vs. renewable capacity growth rate - the gap that forces extraction.

dimensions.title: Planetary Boundaries & Carrying Capacity
dimensions.analysis: Every system has a maximum sustainable extraction rate. Exceeding it causes collapse. We're eating future Earth to feed present Earth.
dimensions.metric: Ecological overshoot - percentage of Earth's regenerative capacity consumed annually (currently ~175%).

dimensions.title: Entropy & the Heat Death Problem
dimensions.analysis: The universe runs on consumption. All life is temporary reversal of entropy, paid for by increasing entropy elsewhere. Galactus is entropy made manifest.
dimensions.metric: Thermodynamic debt - energy borrowed from future states to maintain current complexity.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Galactus must consume planets to survive. Not evil, not good - a fundamental force of nature. Hunger justifies consumption.
vector_entry.business_logic: Resource extraction defended as necessary for survival. Growth imperative overrides externalities. 'We have no choice' economics.
vector_entry.application: Energy policy, extractive industries defense, growth-at-all-costs strategy, resource nationalism, climate change debates

protocol_galactus_heralds.application: Sales compensation design, quota ethics, incentive alignment, principal-agent problems, whistleblower motivations
protocol_galactus_heralds.narrative: Galactus grants incredible power to his Heralds - Silver Surfer, Firelord, Terrax, Air-Walker - in exchange for finding him planets to consume. They receive god-like abilities but must serve as scouts for genocide. Most Heralds eventually rebel when they realize what they're enabling. The Surfer's origin: Norrin Radd sacrifices himself to be Herald, hoping to lead Galactus away from populated worlds, but the Power Cosmic corrupts his empathy over time.
protocol_galactus_heralds.business_translation: Sales teams compensated purely on revenue will sell anything to anyone, regardless of fit. The Wells Fargo fake accounts scandal - reps opening fraudulent accounts to hit quota. Pharma reps pushing opioids to hit numbers. The Herald problem: give someone power and incentives aligned with your hunger, and they'll find ways to feed it, ethics be damned.

dimensions.title: Compensation-Driven Cognitive Dissonance
dimensions.analysis: When your paycheck depends on not understanding something, you won't understand it. Heralds must suppress empathy to function.
dimensions.metric: Ethical disengagement score - measured by ratio of questionable deals to total deals, correlated with commission structure.

dimensions.title: CRM Systems as Hunting Tools
dimensions.analysis: Sales tech optimized to find and convert targets, not to assess mutual benefit. Lead scoring as prey identification.
dimensions.metric: False positive rate - percentage of "qualified leads" that shouldn't have been sold to.

dimensions.title: Principal-Agent Problem in Sales
dimensions.analysis: Salesperson's incentive (commission) misaligned with customer's interest (good fit) and company's interest (sustainable growth). Classic agency problem.
dimensions.metric: Customer lifetime value vs. acquisition cost ratio - negative CLV indicates predatory selling.

dimensions.title: The Corruption of Power
dimensions.analysis: The Power Cosmic slowly erodes the Herald's original values. Power corrupts incrementally - first you compromise once "just this time," then it's your identity.
dimensions.metric: Value drift velocity - rate at which stated values diverge from actual behavior, correlated with power/compensation increases.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Galactus grants god-like power to Heralds who scout planets for consumption. Power and incentives corrupt empathy. Most eventually rebel.
vector_entry.business_logic: Sales compensation purely on revenue drives ethical violations. Wells Fargo fake accounts. Pharma opioid pushing. Incentives corrupt judgment.
vector_entry.application: Sales compensation design, quota ethics, incentive alignment, principal-agent problems, whistleblower motivations

protocol_ultimate_nullifier.business_logic: MAD Doctrine, Nuclear Options, and Reputational Suicide Switches
protocol_ultimate_nullifier.application: Litigation strategy, whistleblower protection, patent portfolio defense, executive departure negotiations, hostile takeover defense
protocol_ultimate_nullifier.narrative: The Ultimate Nullifier is the one weapon Galactus fears. It can erase the wielder, the target, and potentially the entire universe. When Reed Richards threatens to use it, Galactus spares Earth - not because Reed can kill him, but because the Nullifier's use would destroy everything. It's the perfect deterrent: mutual assured destruction. Later, Quasar destroys a cosmic threat with it but disappears from existence in the process.
protocol_ultimate_nullifier.business_translation: The legal strategy where both parties have so much dirt on each other that neither can sue. The employee with the "dead man's switch" email revealing company secrets. Patent trolls with nuclear portfolios. The whistleblower with encrypted files set to auto-release. "If I go down, we all go down." The problem: eventually someone crazy enough to pull the trigger acquires the weapon.

dimensions.title: The Psychology of Brinksmanship
dimensions.analysis: Game theory assumes rational actors, but brinkmanship requires credible willingness to be irrational. You must be believed capable of mutually assured destruction.
dimensions.metric: Credibility coefficient - market belief that you'd actually pull the trigger, measured by negotiation outcomes.

dimensions.title: Dead Man's Switches & Auto-Destruct Protocols
dimensions.analysis: Technical systems that trigger catastrophe if not actively prevented. Encrypted files with dead man timers. The engineering of mutually assured destruction.
dimensions.metric: Trigger sensitivity - how close to automatic activation, balanced against false positive rate.

dimensions.title: Nuclear Option Economics
dimensions.analysis: The market value of credible mutual destruction capability. What's the price of a functioning Ultimate Nullifier? How much to make it non-credible?
dimensions.metric: Deterrence premium - quantified negotiation advantage from credible mutual destruction capability.

dimensions.title: The Irrationality Requirement
dimensions.analysis: Perfect deterrence requires credible threat of irrational action. But if you're truly rational, the threat isn't credible. The paradox of MAD.
dimensions.metric: Rationality boundary - the point at which hyper-rational analysis defeats deterrence by proving threats aren't credible.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Ultimate Nullifier can destroy universe including wielder. Perfect deterrent through mutually assured destruction. Requires credible irrationality.
vector_entry.business_logic: Dead man's switches, legal MAD strategies, whistleblower insurance files, patent nuclear options. 'If I go down, we all go down.'
vector_entry.application: Litigation strategy, whistleblower protection, patent portfolio defense, executive departure negotiations, hostile takeover defense

protocol_thanos_balance.business_logic: The Malthusian Trap & Zero-Sum Resource Allocation
protocol_thanos_balance.application: Corporate restructuring, resource allocation under scarcity, utilitarian ethics in policy, automation displacement, climate population debates
protocol_thanos_balance.narrative: Thanos believes the universe's fundamental problem is overpopulation depleting finite resources. His solution: eliminate exactly half of all life, randomly and fairly. In the comics, he does this to impress Death (literal embodiment). In the MCU, he's a true believer in Malthusian limits. After the Snap, he destroys the Infinity Stones and retires to a farm, his work complete. He views himself as a savior performing necessary triage on a terminal patient.
protocol_thanos_balance.business_translation: The belief that resources are fundamentally limited, so prosperity is zero-sum. Immigration opponents who think more people = fewer jobs. Climate activists arguing population reduction is necessary. Corporate restructuring that slashes headcount 50% to "save the company." The assumption that the pie is fixed, so the only solution is to have fewer mouths to feed.

dimensions.title: Sociopathic Utilitarianism
dimensions.analysis: The psychology of someone who can calculate mass death dispassionately. Effective altruism taken to genocidal extreme. The removal of empathy from decision-making.
dimensions.metric: Empathy deficit disorder score - inability to weight individual suffering in utilitarian calculations.

dimensions.title: Optimization Algorithm Extremism
dimensions.analysis: AI trained purely on efficiency metrics will recommend "Thanos solutions." Algorithms don't have empathy - they have objective functions. Maximize output, minimize input, ignore human cost.
dimensions.metric: Algorithmic cruelty index - inhumane recommendations from efficiency-optimized systems.

dimensions.title: Malthusian Economics vs. Boserupian Innovation
dimensions.analysis: Malthus said population growth outpaces food supply. Boserup said scarcity drives innovation, increasing carrying capacity. Thanos is pure Malthus - ignoring innovation potential.
dimensions.metric: Carrying capacity elasticity - how much innovation increases sustainable population vs. fixed resource assumptions.

dimensions.title: Entropy Acceleration
dimensions.analysis: Thanos doesn't stop entropy, just delays it. Killing half the universe buys maybe a few generations. Then what? The heat death of the universe is inevitable anyway.
dimensions.metric: Problem deferral duration - how long does the "solution" delay the underlying issue before it recurs?

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Thanos believes overpopulation depletes resources. Solution: kill exactly half of all life, randomly. Views genocide as necessary triage.
vector_entry.business_logic: Zero-sum resource thinking. Mass layoffs to 'save the company.' Population control advocacy. Efficiency optimization ignoring human cost.
vector_entry.application: Corporate restructuring, resource allocation under scarcity, utilitarian ethics in policy, automation displacement, climate population debates

protocol_thanos_snap.business_logic: Digital Transformation's Binary Thinking & Cliff-Edge Decisions
protocol_thanos_snap.application: Change management, digital transformation, organizational pivots, policy simplification traps, binary referendums on complex issues
protocol_thanos_snap.narrative: With a snap of his fingers while wearing the Infinity Gauntlet, Thanos erases half of all sentient life in the universe. No targeting, no exceptions, perfectly random. It's the ultimate binary solution - 1 or 0, exist or don't exist. No gradients, no compromises, no nuance. Five years later, the Avengers undo the Snap, but those five years created unfixable complexities - people moved on, remarried, had new families.
protocol_thanos_snap.business_translation: The belief that complex problems need simple solutions. "We'll solve climate change with one weird trick." Cryptocurrency advocates who think blockchain solves all trust issues. The startup that fires the entire sales team to pivot to "product-led growth." Brexit's binary referendum on a complex geopolitical relationship. Any time someone promises a single action will solve a systemic problem.

dimensions.title: The Authoritarian Personality
dimensions.analysis: The psychological comfort of simple answers to complex questions. Intolerance for ambiguity. The seduction of the big red button.
dimensions.metric: Cognitive complexity score - ability to hold multiple contradictory truths. Low score correlates with binary thinking.

dimensions.title: Catastrophic System Shocks
dimensions.analysis: Complex systems don't respond well to instantaneous massive changes. Removing 50% of all life causes cascading failures. Planes crash mid-flight. Nuclear reactors melt down.
dimensions.metric: Resilience to shock - system stability after sudden 50% capacity loss across all nodes.

dimensions.title: The Restoration Paradox
dimensions.analysis: You can't simply "undo" five years. The returned find their homes occupied, spouses remarried, jobs filled. Resurrection creates new problems.
dimensions.metric: Systemic recovery time - duration to restore equilibrium after massive shock and reversal.

dimensions.title: Irreversibility of Time
dimensions.analysis: You can reverse the Snap, but not time. The five years happened. Decisions made in that time can't be unmade. Entropy increased.
dimensions.metric: Temporal paradox density - number of irreconcilable contradictions created by reversal attempts.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: One snap erases half of all life. Binary solution to complex problem. Reversal creates new cascading problems. Simple answers to complex questions.
vector_entry.business_logic: Digital transformation binary thinking. 'One weird trick' solutions. Brexit referendums. Firing entire departments. Pivot-or-die mentality.
vector_entry.application: Change management, digital transformation, organizational pivots, policy simplification traps, binary referendums on complex issues

protocol_thanos_retirement.application: Succession planning, founder transitions, executive retirement programs, post-M&A integration, wealth management for sudden liquidity
protocol_thanos_retirement.narrative: After the Snap, Thanos destroys the Infinity Stones and retires to a peaceful farm planet. He's achieved his life's purpose - and now has nothing to do. When the Avengers find him, he's just... farming. Growing crops. Watching sunsets. His entire identity was built around the quest, and completing it left him empty. He almost seems relieved when they kill him - at least it's an ending.
protocol_thanos_retirement.business_translation: The entrepreneur who sells their company for $100M and then spirals into depression. The executive who retires after a successful career and doesn't know who they are anymore. The athlete who wins the championship and then has an identity crisis. When your entire self-concept is built around achieving a goal, achieving it destroys your purpose.

dimensions.title: Achievement Motivation Collapse

dimensions.title: Heat Death as Telos

protocol_beyonder_godchild.business_translation: The 22-year-old crypto founder with billions in VC money and no adult supervision. The Peter Principle meets omnipotence - promoted to god-level power without god-level judgment.

dimensions.title: Emotional Intelligence Lag

dimensions.metric: Capability-maturity gap - difference between technical power level and emotional intelligence quotient.

dimensions.title: Fast-Scaling Without Governance

dimensions.metric: Governance debt - difference between company scale and institutional maturity, measured by policy coverage gaps.

dimensions.title: Infinite Resources Without Scarcity Discipline
dimensions.analysis: Unlimited funding removes market discipline. The Beyonder has no constraints. SoftBank's $100B Vision Fund. Money that makes people stupid.
dimensions.metric: Capital efficiency degradation - rising CAC and falling ROAS as capital constraints disappear.

dimensions.title: The Omnipotence Paradox
dimensions.analysis: Can God create a rock so heavy he can't lift it? Can the Beyonder learn limitation? Is growth that never encounters resistance actually growth?
dimensions.metric: Constraint encounter frequency - how often unlimited power meets situations it can't solve through force.

protocol_dark_phoenix.business_translation: The executive who becomes a tyrant after success. The company that dominates a market and abuses that dominance. Microsoft's antitrust years. dimensions.title: Addiction Neurology

dimensions.metric: Power-induced empathy decline - measurable drop in perspective-taking as authority increases.

dimensions.title: Platform Dominance & Abuse
dimensions.analysis: Once you're the only game in town, you can extract rents. App Store fees, AWS lock-in, Google search monopoly. Phoenix-level market power enables predation.
dimensions.metric: Monopoly rent extraction - percentage of revenue from anti-competitive practices vs. value creation.

dimensions.title: The Resource Curse
dimensions.analysis: Countries with massive oil wealth often have worse outcomes than resource-poor nations. Too much power/wealth corrupts institutions. Saudi Arabia vs. Singapore.
dimensions.metric: Resource curse coefficient - correlation between resource abundance and governance quality (often negative).

dimensions.title: Power Levels Beyond Mortality
dimensions.analysis: Some capabilities are incompatible with human psychology. You can't be both human and god. The power destroys the container.
dimensions.metric: Ego dissolution threshold - power level at which self-concept fractures under capability weight.

dimensions.metric: Platform dependency risk - percentage of business model dependent on single platform's discretionary decisions.

dimensions.title: Instant Market Contraction
dimensions.analysis: Industry goes from millions of participants to hundreds overnight. No gradual transition, no time to adapt. Creative destruction on fast-forward. Economic trauma.
dimensions.metric: Market shock velocity - rate of industry contraction vs. typical business adaptation timescales.

dimensions.title: Reality as Consensus, Not Constant

dimensions.title: Resource Division Economics
dimensions.analysis: Splitting resources hurts both sides short-term. But maintaining unity while fighting over resources hurts more. Sometimes divorce is efficient despite division costs.
dimensions.metric: Divorce efficiency - combined value of split entities vs. value destruction from continuing civil war.

dimensions.title: Irreconcilable Differences Exist
dimensions.analysis: Not all conflicts have compromise solutions. Some values are truly incompatible. Forcing unity creates worse outcomes than accepting incompatibility.
dimensions.metric: Compromise quality - stakeholder satisfaction with forced unity vs. clean separation when values diverge >X distance.

vector_entry.business_logic: Co-founder ideological split. Google military contracts. Coinbase politics debate. PayPal Mafia divergence. Sometimes split healthier than false unity.

protocol_phoenix_five.application: Governance structure design, power distribution mechanisms, checks and balances implementation, emergency authority protocols, founder agreements
protocol_phoenix_five.narrative: Phoenix Force returns to Earth seeking Hope Summers as host. Avengers want to stop it (Phoenix = danger). X-Men want to embrace it (Phoenix = mutant salvation). Battle on moon shatters Phoenix Force into five pieces, possessing Cyclops, Emma, Namor, Colossus, Magik. Phoenix Five remake world - end hunger, war, create clean energy. But power corrupts. They become authoritarian "benevolent" dictators. Eventually Cyclops absorbs all Phoenix power, becomes Dark Phoenix, kills Professor X. Power concentration = inevitable corruption.
protocol_phoenix_five.business_translation: Multiple co-founders with equal shares seems safe - checks and balances. But during crisis, power concentrates. The CEO who "temporarily" takes emergency powers never gives them back. Board that authorizes "special measures" finds they're permanent. Even starting distributed, pressure toward concentration is immense.

dimensions.title: Power Corruption Acceleration
dimensions.analysis: Absolute power corrupts absolutely, but speed matters. Sudden power corrupts faster than gradual accumulation. Phoenix Five go from heroes to tyrants in weeks.
dimensions.metric: Corruption velocity - time from power acquisition to first abusive decision, faster with sudden vs. gradual power gain.

dimensions.title: Distributed vs. Centralized Architectures
dimensions.analysis: Blockchain's promise of distributed power vs. reality of mining concentration. "No single point of failure" until whales emerge. Distribution is unstable equilibrium.
dimensions.metric: Decentralization decay - Gini coefficient over time in supposedly distributed systems, typically trends toward concentration.

dimensions.title: Benevolent Dictator Economics
dimensions.analysis: Philosopher-king problem. Even well-intentioned autocrats create dependency, stifle markets, prevent price discovery. Phoenix Five solve world problems but make humanity dependent.
dimensions.metric: Autonomy preservation - economic independence and self-determination levels under benevolent vs. malevolent vs. absent authority.

dimensions.title: The Addiction of Doing Good
dimensions.analysis: Helping people is addictive. When you can solve any problem, you must solve every problem. Messiah complex isn't evil - it's the conviction you know what's best.
dimensions.metric: Interventionism escalation - rate at which "helping" justifications expand scope of control.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Phoenix Force splits into five X-Men. They remake world - end hunger, war. But become authoritarian. Power concentrates into Cyclops, who kills Xavier. Distributed power → concentration → corruption.
vector_entry.business_logic: Multiple co-founders with equal shares. But crisis drives concentration. CEO 'temporary' emergency powers become permanent. Distribution unstable, trends to concentration.

protocol_krakoa_nation.business_logic: Platform Monopolies, UBI Economics & Post-Scarcity Implications
protocol_krakoa_nation.application: Platform strategy, post-scarcity economic modeling, UBI policy design, pharmaceutical pricing ethics, monopoly leverage analysis
protocol_krakoa_nation.narrative: Xavier and Magneto create Krakoan nation - sentient island offering mutants citizenship. All mutants welcome, amnesty for past crimes. Krakoa provides housing, food, teleportation via portals. In exchange, mutants manufacture miracle drugs (extending human lifespan) traded to nations for recognition. Resurrection protocols bring back all dead mutants via genetic backups and Phoenix Force. Death becomes temporary. Mutant population explodes. Creates post-scarcity economy but raises questions: What motivates people when needs are met and death is temporary?
protocol_krakoa_nation.business_translation: What happens when AI/automation creates abundance? When basic income guarantees survival? Krakoa is test case for post-work society. Also: using pharmaceutical monopoly (miracle drugs) for geopolitical leverage is exactly what pharma companies do with patents. Nations recognize Krakoa to get drugs, like recognizing China to get manufacturing.

dimensions.title: Post-Scarcity Motivation
dimensions.analysis: Maslow's hierarchy - once survival needs are met, what drives people? Creative expression? Status games? Or do they atrophy? Purpose in post-work world.
dimensions.metric: Engagement in post-scarcity - creative output, community participation when material needs are guaranteed.

dimensions.title: Resurrection Protocol Infrastructure
dimensions.analysis: Backing up consciousness, cloning bodies, reintegrating memories. The technical architecture of defeating death. Equivalent: cloud backups, redundancy, disaster recovery.
dimensions.metric: Recovery time objective - duration from death/failure to full restoration of function.

dimensions.title: Pharmaceutical Monopoly Leverage
dimensions.analysis: Control life-extension drugs = geopolitical power. Same as oil, semiconductors, rare earths. Nations will compromise values for access to crucial resources.
dimensions.metric: Resource monopoly premium - price above marginal cost that monopolist can extract based on essentiality.

dimensions.title: Death as Limitation Removal
dimensions.analysis: Death creates urgency, meaning, stakes. Without it, do choices matter? The "quantum immortality" problem - if all timelines exist, does morality matter?
dimensions.metric: Decision quality with/without stakes - when consequences are reversible, how does risk-taking change?

protocol_five_resurrection.business_logic: Platform Labor & The Gig Economy of Critical Infrastructure
protocol_five_resurrection.application: Essential worker valuation, platform labor ethics, critical infrastructure resilience, service level agreement design, labor dignity in tech
protocol_five_resurrection.narrative: "The Five" are mutants whose combined powers enable resurrection: Egg (creates body), Proteus (shapes it), Elixir (adds life), Hope (boosts powers), Tempus (coordinates timing). They work shifts at "hatchery" bringing back dead mutants from genetic/memory backups. It's factory work - industrial-scale resurrection. They bring back hundreds, thousands. Creates questions: Who gets resurrected first? What about pre-backup memory loss? Is resurrected person truly "them"? Are The Five priests or factory workers?
protocol_five_resurrection.business_translation: The engineers keeping AWS running, content moderators screening trauma, delivery drivers as essential workers. They provide critical infrastructure but treated as factory workers. The Five literally hold power over life and death but work shifts. Essential labor undervalued until crisis. "Resurrection as a Service" is infrastructure-as-a-service metaphor made literal.

dimensions.title: Essential Worker Burnout
dimensions.analysis: The psychological toll of doing critical work repeatedly. Compassion fatigue in healthcare, vicarious trauma in moderators. The Five experience resurrection like assembly line.
dimensions.metric: Burnout incidence in essential workers - emotional exhaustion, depersonalization vs. other worker categories.

dimensions.title: Service Level Agreements for Life
dimensions.analysis: Resurrection becomes expectation, not miracle. SLAs on uptime. What's acceptable resurrection delay? 99.9% uptime = 8.76 hours downtime per year. Acceptable death duration?
dimensions.metric: Platform availability requirements - user tolerance for downtime on critical infrastructure services.

dimensions.title: Pricing Life & Triage Economics
dimensions.analysis: If resurrection capacity is finite, who gets priority? Payment? Status? Random? Healthcare rationing, organ transplant lists. Krakoa doesn't charge but has implicit hierarchy.
dimensions.metric: Allocation mechanisms - efficiency and equity of scarce life-saving resource distribution systems.

dimensions.title: Ship of Theseus Identity Problem
dimensions.analysis: If you replace brain cells one by one, are you still you? Clone body + implanted memories - is that the same person? What is continuity of self?
dimensions.metric: Identity continuity validation - philosophical/legal frameworks for determining "same person" status in reconstructive scenarios.

vector_entry.business_logic: Platform essential workers. AWS engineers, content moderators, delivery drivers. Critical infrastructure undervalued. 'Resurrection as a Service' = infrastructure-as-a-service.

protocol_genosha_apartheid.application: Supply chain ethics, labor exploitation detection, forced labor elimination, human rights due diligence, systemic oppression analysis
protocol_genosha_apartheid.narrative: Genosha appears to be prosperous nation. Secret: powered by enslaved mutants. Mutants detected at birth, stripped of rights, turned into "mutates" - mind-wiped workers. They build the economy, live in camps. Government claims it's for mutants' own good - structure, purpose, safety. Eventually overthrown, becomes mutant haven, then Magneto rules it, then Sentinels genocide 16 million mutants there. The failed state cycle: oppression → revolution → chaos → authoritarianism → genocide.
protocol_genosha_apartheid.business_translation: Company towns, visa-tied foreign workers, prison labor, Uyghur forced labor. "We're giving them jobs/structure/purpose" while extracting value and removing agency. When exploitation is formalized into system, normalized. Genosha is every oppressive labor system claiming benevolence.

dimensions.title: Systemic Dehumanization
dimensions.analysis: Creating underclass requires psychological process of dehumanization. Taught that enslaved group is different, lesser, benefits from subjugation. Apartheid logic.
dimensions.metric: Dehumanization index - social distance, empathy deficit, willingness to harm outgroup vs. ingroup.

dimensions.title: Surveillance & Control Infrastructure
dimensions.analysis: Oppressive systems require technical capacity for tracking, controlling, suppressing. Genosha's mutant detection/control is advanced. Modern equivalent: China's surveillance state.
dimensions.metric: Authoritarian tech capability - surveillance density, control system sophistication vs. human rights outcomes.

dimensions.title: Exploitation-Dependent Economics
dimensions.analysis: When economy is built on cheap/slave labor, reform threatens prosperity. Resistance to change even when morally right. Southern US pre-Civil War. Gulf states today.
dimensions.metric: Economic exploitation dependence - percentage of GDP dependent on undervalued/coerced labor.

dimensions.title: The Failed State Cycle
dimensions.analysis: Oppression creates resistance. Revolution creates chaos. Chaos creates authoritarianism. Authoritarianism creates oppression. Breaking cycle requires external intervention or revolutionary wisdom (rare).
dimensions.metric: Cycle completion time - duration from oppression through revolution back to oppression (typically 1-2 generations).

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Genosha powered by enslaved mutants. Mutates mind-wiped for labor. Appears prosperous but built on oppression. Eventually overthrown, cycles through chaos to authoritarianism.
vector_entry.business_logic: Labor exploitation as 'opportunity.' Company towns, visa-tied workers, prison labor, Uyghur forced labor. System normalized. Extraction disguised as benevolence.

protocol_genosha_genocide.application: Industry transition support, workforce retraining, just transition policies, market disruption ethics, collective trauma response
protocol_genosha_genocide.narrative: Cassandra Nova sends Sentinels to Genosha. They systematically exterminate 16 million mutants in hours. Not a battle - a genocide. Sentinels are efficient, thorough, merciless. Genosha goes from mutant haven to graveyard. Few survivors. The trauma defines next generation of X-Men stories. Emma Frost survives in diamond form, surrounded by corpses. The world barely notices - 16 million mutants dead, page 12 news.
protocol_genosha_genocide.business_translation: Entire industries destroyed overnight. Blockbuster by Netflix. Taxi medallions by Uber. Coal jobs by natural gas/renewables. Kodak by digital cameras. The market doesn't mourn - it moves on. Workers in dead industries are statistics. Creative destruction is brutal for those destroyed. Survivors have PTSD. World keeps spinning.

dimensions.title: Collective Trauma & Survivor Guilt
dimensions.analysis: Genocide survivors carry permanent psychological scars. Why did I survive? Could I have saved others? The mental health crisis in post-genocide populations.
dimensions.metric: Intergenerational trauma transmission - PTSD incidence in genocide survivors and their children vs. baseline.

dimensions.title: Industrialized Killing Efficiency
dimensions.analysis: Genosha genocide used autonomous weapons. Modern equivalent: AI-enabled warfare, drone swarms. Technology makes mass killing "clean" for perpetrators.
dimensions.metric: Casualty efficiency - deaths per perpetrator hour, increases with technological sophistication.

dimensions.title: Market Indifference to Suffering
dimensions.analysis: Markets are amoral. Industry disruption creates losers but capital flows to winners. 16 million mutant deaths barely affect stock markets. Efficiency doesn't care about suffering.
dimensions.metric: Disruption empathy gap - market reaction to efficiency gains vs. humanitarian costs of disruption.

dimensions.title: Evil Banality & Automation
dimensions.analysis: Hannah Arendt's "banality of evil." Genocide doesn't require monsters - just bureaucrats following orders. Sentinels are perfect metaphor: programmed genocide, no malice.
dimensions.metric: Automation of harm - correlation between process automation and perpetrator psychological distance from consequences.

vector_entry.narrative_summary: Sentinels exterminate 16 million mutants in Genosha in hours. Systematic, efficient genocide. World barely notices. Survivors traumatized. Haven to graveyard instantly.
vector_entry.business_logic: Industry extinction events. Blockbuster/Netflix, Taxis/Uber, Coal/renewables, Kodak/digital. Market doesn't mourn. Workers are statistics. Creative destruction's brutality.

protocol_legacy_virus.application: Pandemic preparedness, pharmaceutical pricing policy, rare disease research funding, healthcare resource allocation, crisis sacrifice ethics
protocol_legacy_virus.narrative: Stryfe (Cable's clone) unleashes Legacy Virus - disease targeting mutants, eventual human crossover potential. Symptoms similar to AIDS. No cure initially. Mutants die slowly, publicly. Human governments delay research funding. Some humans celebrate "mutant disease." Beast races for cure but faces ethical dilemmas: human testing, triage, resource allocation. Cure eventually requires sacrifice - Colossus kills himself to release cure into atmosphere. Disease as weapon, as metaphor, as resource allocation crisis.
protocol_legacy_virus.business_translation: COVID-19 revealed every dynamic: government funding delays, treatment rationing, vaccine nationalism, price gouging, sacrifice of healthcare workers. Martin Shkreli raising drug prices 5000%. AIDS crisis funding delays. Rare disease research economics. When do we fund cures vs. let markets decide?

dimensions.title: Disease Stigma & Social Death
dimensions.analysis: Legacy Virus carriers face discrimination, isolation, fear. Social death before biological death. Same as AIDS stigma, leprosy historically. Disease becomes moral judgment.
dimensions.metric: Stigma severity - employment discrimination, social isolation, violence against disease carriers vs. actual transmission risk.

dimensions.title: Research Prioritization Algorithms
dimensions.analysis: How do we allocate research funding? Mortality? Economic impact? Political pressure? Legacy Virus delayed because mutants are minority. Rare disease problem.
dimensions.metric: Research funding equity - dollars per DALY (disability-adjusted life year) across diseases, shows political/economic bias.

dimensions.title: Pharmaceutical Pricing Power
dimensions.analysis: When cure exists but is unaffordable, market has failed. Insulin pricing. Epipen gouging. Orphan drug costs. Legacy cure required sacrifice, not payment.
dimensions.metric: Essential medicine access gap - percentage of patients who need treatment vs. percentage who can afford it.

dimensions.title: Sacrifice Ethics
dimensions.analysis: Colossus's suicide to release cure - is it noble or systemic failure that someone had to die? Should cures require martyrs? Healthcare worker COVID deaths.
dimensions.metric: Essential worker mortality premium - death rate in critical roles during crisis vs. baseline population.

protocol_quiet_council.application: Board composition design, stakeholder governance authenticity, ESG oversight credibility, democratic governance preservation, oligarchy prevention
protocol_quiet_council.narrative: Krakoa governed by Quiet Council - 12 mutants representing different factions (Xavier, Magneto, Apocalypse, Sinister, Emma, etc.). Consensus-based but includes literal villains. Laws passed include "Murder no man" (except humans invading Krakoa), "Make more mutants," "Respect the sacred land." Council has absolute authority but claims democratic legitimacy. Citizens have no vote. It's oligarchy with democratic aesthetics. Sinister on the council (known for genetics crimes) is like war criminals in government.
protocol_quiet_council.business_translation: Corporate boards claim stakeholder representation but are selected by existing board/CEO. ESG committees with fossil fuel execs. "Independent" directors who are friends of CEO. Facebook's oversight board. The governance theater - claiming democratic legitimacy while concentrating power. Including "reformed" bad actors because they have resources/knowledge.

dimensions.title: Oligarchic Psychology & Elite Capture
dimensions.analysis: Small groups making decisions "for" large populations develop disconnected worldview. Davos attendees solving world problems. Elite consensus ≠ popular will.
dimensions.metric: Elite-population preference gap - policy positions of decision-makers vs. constituent populations they claim to represent.

dimensions.title: Governance Theater Technology
dimensions.analysis: The technical infrastructure of fake democracy. Voting systems that don't matter. Consultation processes ignored. Comment periods performative. Algorithms creating illusion of voice.
dimensions.metric: Governance efficacy - correlation between constituent input and actual decisions made by governing body.

dimensions.title: Oligopolistic Cartel Behavior
dimensions.analysis: When council includes competitors, it's collusion. Sinister, Apocalypse, Xavier supposedly competing philosophies but coordinating. OPEC, tech companies "competing" while coordinating on labor.
dimensions.metric: Coordination evidence - price/policy correlation among supposed competitors beyond chance.

dimensions.title: Democratic Backsliding Mechanisms
dimensions.analysis: How democracies become authoritarian: concentrate power in crisis, never release it. "Emergency" becomes permanent. Krakoa founded during existential threat, emergency powers now normal.
dimensions.metric: Democratic erosion indicators - civil liberties, press freedom, electoral integrity over time under "temporary" concentrated authority.
